Parked as a note so the idea isn't lost, not a build item. SETTLED 2026-08-02: BL-157 (settled today) already covers the data half — it positions a unit by TILE ID, and a coastal tile is a tile, so a naval base or coastal-defense unit needs NO schema change at all. That was the anxiety behind filing the stub, and it is answered for free. What remains is genuinely a mechanic (shore bombardment, blockade, contested landings) which is Conflict proper and excluded from the prototype, so it STAYS PARKED with an updated revisit trigger: no longer "BL-157 lands" (satisfied) but "Conflict proper enters active design". Not closed, because the idea that coastal tiles carry a military identity is captured nowhere else and BL-188 covers only their commercial half.

items.title: Food consumption model — plain market demand, no starvation mechanic
items.summary: Filed + settled 2026-07-21 (design session, Ben), closing an assumption this session's BL-166/168 design wrongly carried — that off-world/coastal food production needs a not-yet-built population consumer. Ben's call: population food demand is (and stays) a **plain market-demand pull**, never a starvation/health/death mechanic; Food rations arrive later as the tier-2 good the demand eventually targets.

items.title: Endemic trade goods - the mercantile value track (C -> D)
items.summary: A fourth resource VALUE TRACK (mercantile) alongside industrial/ambient/habitability: endemic goods whose value comes from geography rather than utility. Generated by the biosphere in a new C -> D chain stage, bound to a latitude band AND a longitude sector, and priced per-market by distance from where they grow. Landed 2026-07-22.

items.title: Gameplay affordances that generation only sometimes produces (highways, player processing facility)
items.summary: Deferred. Two measured cases where world generation produces a gameplay-relevant affordance only in a minority of worlds: the highway road tier (~37% of worlds have none) and the player opening with a processing facility (~25% of seeds). Both are pre-existing generation behaviour, surfaced by BL-167 measurement, not caused by it. Question is whether such affordances should be guaranteed, made more likely, or designed around. SETTLED 2026-08-02 (measurement gate already discharged at 37%/25%): case 1 (highways) takes option (c) design-around — a world without highways is a legible starting condition and makes road tiers mean something regionally; no generation change. Case 2 (player processing facility) takes NEITHER guarantee NOR retune — both are the forced-outcome clamping Ben rejected in BL-167, and retuning a distribution to serve a UI flow silently changes everything else it drives. Instead REMOVE THE DEPENDENCY: US-007 does not need the player to OWN a processor at t=0, it needs them to reach one, and BL-162 construction ledger has landed, so the build-then-steer path is the answer. What is worth measuring instead is whether a fresh campaign has the capital and sited opportunity to build one early — a different and much cheaper question. UNPARKED F->C: this is a live onboarding gap in three quarters of campaigns with a small resolution.
items.design:
**Deferred (parked, F).** Surfaced during BL-167/BL-191 (2026-07-22) but explicitly NOT caused by them — both are pre-existing behaviour of population/road/corporation generation that only became visible once the default world changed and the harnesses started measuring across seeds. Ben: "we can work on the third issue waiting for me if it is a problem later."

**The shared shape.** Generation produces a gameplay-relevant affordance only in a minority of worlds, and a check or a player flow quietly depends on it. Neither case is a bug in the generator; both are an unstated assumption about what every world provides.

**Case 1 — the highway road tier. ~37% of worlds have none.** `edge_tier` (road_generation.cpp) returns Highway only when BOTH endpoints of a road edge are scale >= 3 (City+). Population scale is drawn from a fixed weighted distribution (40/30/20/8/2 for scales 1-5, population_generation.cpp), so ~30% of centres are City+ — but whether any such PAIR ends up adjacent in the road graph is spatial luck. Measured: highways present on 3 of 8 seeds. This broke `road_generation_harness` R2, which asserted the tier existed in one specific world; the check now asserts the tier is REACHABLE across seeds instead (a fragile assertion made honest, not weakened — had no seed produced one it would still fail).

**Case 2 — the player's opening processing facility. ~25% of seeds.** `scripts/verify/recipe_workforce.lua` realises US-007 ("steer a building's recipe and workforce") and needs the player to own a `processing_facility`; corporation generation only gives them one on some seeds. Measured by planetology_harness R11: 3 of 12 seeds (0x3C6EF362, 0xB54CDA26, 0x538453D7). The script now pins a known-good seed via the new `verify.new_world(seed)` binding, and R11 guards that such seeds keep existing. But it means **three quarters of campaigns open with no building whose production the player can steer**, which is a core Layer-3/4 flow.

**The design question (not settled here).** For each affordance, one of:
  (a) **Guarantee it** — post-process generation to ensure at least one (e.g. promote a centre pair to City scale; ensure the player corp's opening holdings include a processor). Cheapest to reason about, but it is exactly the "forced" clamping Ben rejected for the homeworld in BL-167, so it needs the same scrutiny.
  (b) **Raise the probability** — retune the scale-weight distribution or the corp focus mix so the affordance is common without being certain. Keeps generation honest; needs measurement to pick a target rate.
  (c) **Design around it** — accept that some worlds have no highways and some players start with only extractors, and make that a legible starting condition rather than a missing feature. Most interesting, and consistent with the BL-167 position that failure is content — but the UI must then not present an empty flow as if it were broken.

**Method note.** Whichever is chosen, MEASURE FIRST (the BL-167 pattern): the sweep harness shape (`tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp`) is the model — report the rate, then decide the target, rather than tuning blind.

**Related:** BL-132 (population/market co-generation, which would move population placement and so change case 1's rate), CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 3 (the lean focus-coherent holdings that drive case 2), USER_STORIES.md US-007.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — (c) design around for case 1; for case 2, REMOVE THE DEPENDENCY rather than guarantee it

The measurement the method note demands is **already done** (37% and 25%, across measured seed
sets), so the gate the item sets for itself is discharged and the decision can be taken.

### Case 1 — highways (~37% of worlds): option (c), design around. Nothing is wrong.

A world whose population centres never happen to put two City+ settlements adjacent is a world
without highways, and that is a **legible starting condition**, not a missing feature. It is
also good: it makes the road tiers mean something regionally instead of appearing everywhere.

The harness change already made was the right one and should be read as the model — an assertion
that the tier is *reachable across seeds* is honest, where asserting it exists in one world was
fragile. **No generation change.**

### Case 2 — the player's opening processing facility (~25%): neither (a) nor (b). Remove the dependency.

This case is genuinely different and the item is right to be uneasy: it is not "some worlds lack
a feature", it is "**three quarters of campaigns cannot exercise a core Layer-3/4 flow**"
(US-007, steer a building's recipe and workforce). That is an onboarding failure, not variety.

But (a) **guarantee** is the forced-outcome clamping Ben rejected for the homeworld in BL-167,
and it would be the same mistake for the same reason — reshaping an outcome so a check passes.
(b) **retune** is clamping with extra steps: moving a distribution until a specific affordance
becomes common is tuning generation to serve a UI flow, and it silently changes every other
property that distribution drives.

**The real answer is that the flow should not depend on the player OWNING a processor at
start.** It depends on the player being able to *reach* one — and construction already exists
(BL-162's tile construction ledger landed). A player who opens with only extractors can **build**
a processing facility, and US-007 is reachable by the ordinary build path.

So the fix is not in generation at all: it is to stop treating "player owns a processor at t=0"
as the precondition. Where a genuine gap remains is whether a fresh campaign has the *capital*
and the *sited opportunity* to build one early — that is worth measuring, and it is a different
question with a much cheaper answer than reshaping world generation.

**This keeps generation honest**, which is the whole BL-167 position, and it removes the
dependency rather than engineering around it.

### Consequence for the verify script

`recipe_workforce.lua` pinning a known-good seed stays correct — a check should exercise the
flow deterministically. What changes is that it is no longer standing in for a guarantee the
player experience needs; a second check exercising the **build-then-steer** path is the one that
matches how most campaigns will actually reach US-007.

**Unparked to C.** The original F rested on this being a "problem later"; case 2 is a live
onboarding gap in three quarters of campaigns, and the resolution is small.

items.title: Building stacks on one tile: the richness-derived cap, shared output, and depletion
items.summary: Several buildings may stand on one tile, capped by the tile's resource richness. The cap's shape landed with the building Selection element (placement_rules::stack_capacity, enforced via slot_full) but its constant is a placeholder and the economics are unsettled: stacked extraction sites currently each draw full nominal output from one shared reserve, multiplying output and depletion with no diminishing return. Settle output-sharing, the richness curve, and stack depletion.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-26 (AI design session; drafted by Claude, ratified by Ben same day).** Answers to the three open questions:

1. **Diminishing per-site output, honest shared depletion.** Site k in a stack (stored order, oldest first) produces `base_rate x richness x workforce x d^(k-1)` with **d = 0.8**. Stacking pays sub-linearly (2 sites = 1.8x, 5 sites = 3.36x, never 5x) while each site draws real reserve for what it extracts - so a full stack drains the deposit faster than its output multiple, making stack-vs-spread a genuine trade-off against transport and land rather than a dominant strategy. No clamps, no fake caps: the curve is the economics.

2. **Capacity curve stays richness/50, min 1** (0-250 band -> 1-5 sites) - retained deliberately: with diminishing returns carrying the economics, the cap is a *legibility* bound (how many markers a tile can host), not the balance lever. k_richness_per_site is promoted from placeholder to settled constant; revisit only if the marginal-site curve proves mistuned in play.

3. **Depletion taper is computed against the stack's combined nominal.** Aggregate the per-tile (type, target) stack's nominal draw; every member sees the same taper band and exhausts together (today each site tapers against its own nominal, so stack members desynchronise). run_extraction gains a per-tile stack pre-pass; deterministic, stored-order.

4. **Non-extraction stacking stays capacity 1 in this item.** Whether processors stack on land/workforce/road-tier is a different question - deferred, noted in the item, not blocked on.

**AI relevance (why now).** The BL-202 siting scorer prices the marginal site: `value(site N+1) = base x d^N x margin` - the same curve that stops the AI (and the player) from mindlessly stacking the one best tile. **Authority** -> docs/economy/PRODUCTION.md (stacking is a production rule) on landing; placement_rules.cpp + economy_system.cpp (run_extraction stack pre-pass) + selection_panel.cpp readout.

items.title: AI opponent — research + architecture proposal for a competent, human-skill computer player
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-23 (Ben, SSS). Ben's call: AI-opponent development can now proceed ALONGSIDE basic mechanics rather than waiting. This is the research + design spike that precedes any build: understand how Io actually plays, how grand-strategy-MP AI is normally built, and how to SIMPLIFY that into an opponent of roughly HUMAN skill (competent and beatable, not superhuman, not a handicapped pushover). items.title: Dwell-to-open - holding the pointer still over an entity opens the sticky detail card
items.summary: The owed refinement to the sticky detail card (BL-194/196): the card gains a SECOND opener alongside the click. Holding the pointer STILL over an entity fills a small progress bar at the cursor; when it completes, the card opens on that entity - the pointer-driven twin of click-to-open. Ben's settled call (2026-07-23): a click STILL opens the card instantly; dwell is the additional hover opener, not a replacement. Anti-bombardment: the dwell timer advances only while the mouse holds still, so sweeping the pointer across the dense tile grid never auto-opens. The progress bar lives in the nested hover tooltip, not the card header. Scoped to the Planetary surface, where the hover infrastructure (hover_ticks + draw_hover_card) and the tile-density bombardment problem both live; click-to-open is unchanged on every canvas.

items.title: Corporate border data-model foundation (slice of BL-182) - persisted HQ + influence range, border render off real data
items.summary: The in-scope, deterministic first slice of BL-182 (Ben's 2026-07-23 'Foundation only' call): give the corporate border a real data model instead of a render-time recompute. corporation_component gains a persisted HQ (the seat = holding nearest the holdings centroid on the home body) and an influence_range (holdings extent + a fixed projected reach, in unit-hex distance), both designated deterministically at generation. The Planetary border render (player home-ring BL-085 + rival reach rings BL-183) is unified onto a single lambda that reads this persisted data, drawn on each corp's home body. Gates nothing, mutates no sim state - the operate-gate gameplay mechanic stays deferred in BL-182 (post-v0.1.0).

items.title: Corp AI stage A — scored utility layer over the agency seam, via the corp-command seam
items.summary: Stage A of the accepted AI architecture (BL-199, AI_OPPONENT.md §5-6): grow the BL-079 reflex block into a scored strategic layer. Each AI corp, on a staggered deterministic cadence, enumerates bounded candidates over the player-grade verb set (build / demolish / set_recipe / set_workforce via the BL-181 solver / idle / dispatch_convoy / place_road / survey), scores them with existing estimators (estimate_building_profit, placement affinities, live prices), applies hysteresis (do-nothing bias, cooldowns, streaks) and an action budget, and emits corp_command records applied at the tick boundary through player-grade validation - no bypass, no cheats. The command stream + score rationale is retained as the decision log (ring buffer): the AI legibility surface, the replay artifact, the BL-204 harness input, and the BL-205 chat feed. Includes the visibility-honest compact state export (JSON, versioned) for future out-of-process policies. Difficulty 5 - promote as multiple tasks (command seam; candidate enumeration; scorer; decision log/export).

items.title: Corp AI stage B — strategy layer, priority buckets, predictive spending (the solvency answer)
items.summary: Stage B of the accepted architecture (AI_OPPONENT.md §2B): the Victoria-3 import that makes the AI genuinely solvent instead of handed resources. Adds (1) a strategy layer - each AI corp holds a coarse strategy (extraction specialist / processing / trade arbitrage) derived from its generated industrial focus, biasing the BL-202 scorer; (2) priority buckets - Must-Have (wages, maintenance, debt service) > Should-Have (input feed for running processors) > Nice-to-Have (expansion), where a lower bucket may never starve a higher one; (3) predictive spending - before committing a build, forecast its market impact (post-completion supply delta vs current demand at the local market) so the AI does not over-build into its own glut. Replaces BL-202's crude reserve-floor solvency gate. Difficulty 4.

items.title: AI skill-regression harness — seed-set bot-vs-bot goldens + tick-boundary state hash
items.summary: The data-strategy instrument (AI_OPPONENT.md §3): freeze a benchmark seed-set spanning body/terrain/market diversity; run headless bot-vs-bot rollouts; assert the AI holds its bands (solvency rate, net-worth curve, survival) as regression goldens - the AI analogue of verifier-headless, run on every AI change. Also lands the tick-boundary STATE HASH (a deterministic checksum over the econ-tick snapshot, the parked MULTIPLAYER_PRINCIPLES.md idea): today a two-runs-same-seed regression primitive for this harness, later the lockstep desync detector - one small addition serving both worlds. Authorise as a new verifier-headless check (tools/verify/ai_skill_harness.cpp) per the tool-creation-is-skill-creation rule.

items.title: Corp chat log — replace the Explorer with a channel-based message surface (diplomacy as communication)
items.summary: Ben's call (2026-07-26): since every rival is AI, inter-corp coordination should happen in a communication medium, not hidden state - corps message publicly or in private groups to form plans; diplomacy is legible messaging (AI_OPPONENT.md §7). The surface: a chat log window replacing the Explorer placeholder (right shell band; pinning was never wired - superseded, not lost). Channels: Public (all corps) + arbitrary player-created groups (any corp subset). FIRST SLICE (landed with this filing, 2026-07-26): the window swap, channel tabs + group creation, and a deterministic agency-event feed - the BL-079 reflex actions (recipe rescue, idle-a-loser) post templated messages to Public via a new agency_event vector on economy_report, making the chat the AI-observability surface immediately. Player message input posts to the selected channel (no mechanical effect yet - the C-route hook). LATER: BL-202 command-stream messages; C-route in-character LLM chat; AI-AI private groups + intercept mechanics (Discovery extension).

items.title: World history log — an append-only narrative substrate replacing the per-eval blackboard snapshot (enables a past-history game mode)
items.summary: Ben's pivot (2026-07-28), reacting to BL-206's snapshot-style blackboard export: re-deriving a fresh state summary from the world every time someone reads it is 'unnecessary and boring overhead.' Proposal: make the append-only EVENT LOG the source of truth from world generation onward, not a per-eval snapshot query. Concretely, the bones already exist and are scattered: corp_ai's decision ring (corp_decision_ring) is already an event log of AI commands; trade_routes (last_tick, convoy_count) is already history, not state; agency_event is already a live narrated feed; and PLANETOLOGY.md's per-body dated biography (S0-S9, already implemented under BL-167 - abiogenesis at S5 Spark, the oxygenation bottlenecks at S6 Breath, land colonisation at S7 Green) is already exactly 'how chemical life started and what evolution bottlenecks led to humans forming,' produced once at generation and never revisited. This item unifies those into one growing, replayable log spanning generation through simulation, with the corp_ai blackboard snapshot and the BL-206 JSONL export becoming a DERIVED VIEW over the log rather than an authored artifact. The payoff Ben named: a game can start reading the log from tick 0 instead of 'now,' which is most of what a 'play through the past' mode needs, close to free once the log is the substrate. SETTLED 2026-08-02 (all five): consumers keep querying a DERIVED SNAPSHOT (the item own recommendation — the snapshot becomes disposable and the personas extract() contract does not change at all; deltas-since-last-read makes every consumer stateful for a capability nothing has asked for). Storage is a SINGLE INTERLEAVED world log, append-only, tagged and serialised — per-body/per-corp logs both fail on a corporation acting on a body, which is every interesting event, and joining them needs a global ordering separate logs lack; this shape is already committed because BL-217 deliberately made checkpoint records migrate into it as a move. PLANETOLOGY dated lines merge as the genesis chapter on their existing BL-220 timestamps. The past game mode is PASSIVE READBACK only — a played-through interstitial campaign is an entire second game mode and must not ride along on a logging item. GENERATION_LEDGER stays separate on LIFETIME: the ledger is disposable and tuning-scoped, the log is durable and narrative-scoped, and merging forces one lifetime on both.

items.title: Molecular event trace for abiogenesis — full chemical-synthesis-to-DNA log per body, persisted binary, hex-inspectable, chemical-name display
items.summary: DESIGNED 2026-07-28. Promotes the chemistry currently sitting in COMMENTS at planetology.cpp S5/S6 into a generated, branching, inspectable molecular event trace. S5 Spark today is one boolean emitting one history line; this decomposes it into seven independently-failing gates (Feedstock / Reductant / Phosphorylation / Concentration / Replicator / Compartment / Code) running chemical-synthesis -> RNA -> DNA, and puts a cofactor fork in front of S6's existing flux-balance test. The highest-value piece: the PHOTOSYSTEM FORK (anoxygenic photoferrotrophy vs oxygenic Z-scheme, gated on manganese for the Mn4CaO5 complex) converts PLANETOLOGY.md's own named 'Known weaknesses' uncertainty — whether banded iron gates on life or on oxygen — from a constant into a generated branch. Several gates reach BACK into S0-S4 rolls (S1's late veneer now feeds S5a's impact-reducing atmosphere and S5c's schreibersite phosphorus), which is what makes generation read as one causal system rather than ten independent dice. Adds 3 archetypes (Silent Eden, RNA Lock, Ferrotroph World). Storage is 8-byte fixed-width flat-binary events referencing compiled-in species/reaction tables — ids never strings, so hex is purely a dev display encoding and canonical chemical names resolve through the same table any player surface uses (~500 bytes/body). Q&A 2026-07-28 settled: generative full 7-gate chain (not explanatory-only), new archetypes, drill-down behind the untouched eight-line biography, and design-now/build-after-BL-208.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-28 (Ben, Q&A). Four calls settled: (a) GENERATIVE, FULL 7-GATE CHAIN - every sub-gate can fail independently and change the endowment, not merely narrate an existing verdict; (b) NEW ARCHETYPES added rather than folding new outcomes into the existing 13; (c) surfaced as a DRILL-DOWN behind the eight-line biography, which stays exactly as-is (PLANETOLOGY.md's eight-line cap is load-bearing - the brevity of a failed world IS its characterisation); (d) DESIGN NOW, BUILD AFTER BL-208, so the trace is authored as entries in the append-only world log rather than a parallel per-body structure.

## The problem being solved

S5 Spark is currently ONE BOOLEAN at planetology.cpp:780 - `cycling_venue && geology >= low && time_budget && rng < abiogenesis_ease` - emitting one history line. All the real chemistry (serpentinisation H2, the 0.1 M HCN threshold, Fe(Ni)S walls matching ferredoxin) lives in COMMENTS, not in data. This item promotes that chemistry into a generated, branching, inspectable trace.

## S5 decomposed into seven gates

Each reads inputs already computed by earlier stages, tests one threshold, and has a distinct failure state. Several reach BACK into S0-S4 rolls, which is the point: it makes generation read as one causal system rather than ten independent dice.

| Gate | Question | Key chemistry | Reads from | Fails into |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S5a Feedstock | Anything to build with? | HCN -> purines (adenine is literally (HCN)5); HCHO -> sugars via formose. Yield collapses orders of magnitude in an oxidised CO2/N2 atmosphere vs a reduced one. Modern resolution: IMPACT-GENERATED TRANSIENT REDUCING ATMOSPHERES - a large iron-rich impactor reduces H2O to H2 for ~10^5-10^6 yr (Zahnle, Genda). | S2 atmosphere class; **S1 late-veneer roll**; UV flux | sterile - no organic feedstock, ever |
| S5b Reductant | Free energy of the right shape? | Serpentinisation: olivine + H2O -> serpentine + magnetite + H2, exothermic. Lost City runs 45-90 C, pH 9-11, up to 200 mM H2. Alkaline effluent into a CO2-acidified ocean = a 3-4 pH-unit gradient of the same polarity every living cell uses, across Fe(Ni)S walls. | S3 geology; S4 liquid water; ultramafic crust from S1 | prebiotic - feedstock present, nothing to cycle it |
| S5c Phosphorylation | Could it make a nucleotide? | The genuinely hard one. Seawater P ~1 uM, locked in apatite. Two routes: SCHREIBERSITE (Fe3P from iron meteorites) corroding to reactive phosphite; or CARBONATE-RICH ALKALINE LAKES where Ca drops out as carbonate, freeing P to concentrate ~10^5-10^6x (Toner & Catling). | **S1 metallic impactors** (schreibersite); **S4 subaerial relief + evaporation** (lakes) | NEW: monomers, no nucleotides - sugars and bases exist, nothing links them |
| S5d Concentration | Dense enough to polymerise? | HCN oligomerises above ~0.1 M, competes with hydrolysis at 0.01-0.1 M, loses below. Hadean ocean HCN was orders of magnitude under. 'The ocean was a soup' is chemically false. Venues: wet-dry cycling in subaerial pools (dehydration drives condensation - polymerisation in bulk water is uphill), or hydrothermal pore thermophoresis (~5000x, Braun & Mast), which works WITHOUT land. | S4 water_fraction, relief; S3 geology | prebiotic - today's outcome, now with a named cause |
| S5e Replicator | Did a polymer copy itself AND survive? | THE NEW PHYSICS: an RNA temperature ceiling. The phosphodiester backbone hydrolyses, and the rate climbs steeply with temperature - order-of-magnitude, hours at ~100 C against years near 0 C; cytosine deamination is worse. This sets up a DIRECT ANTAGONISM WITH S5b: vents give the reductant and the gradient, and vents are hot. Lost City at 45-90 C is survivable; a black smoker at 350 C is not. | S4 surface_temp_k; vent temp from S3 theta; S5d venue | NEW: polymers, no replicator - 'chemistry got further here than anywhere else, and stopped' |
| S5f Compartment | Did it become an individual? | Fatty-acid vesicles self-assemble above a critical concentration; without one, a useful ribozyme's benefit diffuses to its competitors and there is no Darwinian individuality. Known unresolved tension: fatty-acid membranes are destabilised by divalent cations, and RNA catalysis REQUIRES Mg2+. Chelators (citrate) are the proposed workaround. | ocean divalent-cation load, from S4 weathering + S1 crust | NEW: replicators, no cells |
| S5g Code | Did it lift the genome ceiling? | RNA -> coded protein (the ribosome is itself a ribozyme) -> DNA via ribonucleotide reductase. The real constraint is EIGEN'S ERROR THRESHOLD: without proofreading, max genome length ~ 1/(per-base mutation rate), capping an RNA-only replicator near a few thousand bases. DNA plus a proofreading polymerase lifts that by orders of magnitude. | S5e fidelity; time budget; cofactors | NEW: RNA LOCK - real, metabolising, evolving life, permanently simple |

**S5f is the weakest of the seven on the 'name the decision' test** - its failure state is exotic and its downstream endowment is identical to S5e's. It is included because Ben chose the full chain, but it is explicitly THE FIRST CANDIDATE TO CUT if tuning shows it never fires distinctly from S5e.

## S6 - the photosystem fork (the highest-value piece)

This converts a named uncertainty in PLANETOLOGY.md's own 'Known weaknesses' into a GENERATED BRANCH instead of a constant. The doc says the BIF oxidant is 'genuinely unresolved between cyanobacterial O2, anoxygenic photoferrotrophy (which needs no free oxygen at all) and abiotic UV photo-oxidation, AND IT DECIDES WHETHER BIF GATES ON LIFE OR ON OXYGEN' - which is what the whole iron/coal antagonism hangs on.

- **S6a Anoxygenic photosynthesis (photoferrotrophy).** One photosystem, Fe(II) as electron donor, no O2 produced. Cheap - fires on nearly any microbial world with dissolved iron. **Precipitates banded iron with NO free oxygen at all.**
- **S6b Oxygenic photosynthesis.** Splitting water needs +1.23 V, more than any single photosystem delivers - which is why it needs TWO chained in series (the Z-scheme), and why it evolved exactly once in 4 Gyr on Earth. Its cofactor is the Mn4CaO5 oxygen-evolving complex, so it GATES ON MANGANESE. Requires the genome headroom from S5g (two photosystems + dozens of genes is not reachable under an RNA-world error threshold).
- **S6c Nitrogen fixation.** N2's 941 kJ/mol triple bond yields only to nitrogenase, whose cofactor is Mo - soluble in oxic water, NOT in anoxic sulfidic water. Low Mo -> weak fixation -> capped productivity -> capped burial -> capped oxygen; and since S8 already states soil requires biological nitrogen fixation, **Mo gates arable_share through pure chemistry.**

The existing GOE / Boring Billion / NOE flux-balance structure runs UNDERNEATH this, unchanged. The cofactor gates sit in front of it.

**Mo and P stay INTERNAL SCALARS, never resources** - this deliberately does not touch PLANETOLOGY.md open call 3 (resource-list expansion), which would shift resource_count and every std::array width in the model.

## New archetypes (13 -> 16)

| Archetype | Died at | Has | Lacks |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Silent Eden** | S5c or S5e, on an otherwise perfect world | oceans, continents, mild climate, pristine ore unweathered by life, clay, sand | ALL fossil carbon, all biology, and - via S8's nitrogen-fixation requirement - **soil: land you cannot farm despite perfect climate** |
| **RNA Lock** | S5g | a real microbial biosphere, marine organics, some BIF | any complexity, any oxygen, any path forward |
| **Ferrotroph World** | S6b (cofactor/genome), with S6a fired | colossal UNBOUNDED banded iron - the window never closes | oxygen, permanently and structurally |

**Silent Eden is the most valuable of the three.** Today a perfect wet world that never sparked resolves to relict_wet, which is WRONG - relict_wet is Mars, a world that lost its air. A living-capable world that stayed silent is a different thing entirely and the current model cannot name it.

**Honest risk on Ferrotroph World:** it may be indistinguishable from Mat World to a player. Both read iron-rich and anoxic. The real difference is causal - Mat World failed on FLUX BALANCE (the reductant flux won, and falling theta could in principle have fixed it), Ferrotroph failed on BIOCHEMISTRY (it never built the water-splitting complex; there is no path). Differentiate them mechanically by giving Ferrotroph a strictly higher, never-closing iron window, plus its own blurb. If tuning cannot separate them, fold Ferrotroph into Mat World rather than shipping two names for one feeling.

## Data model

The compression insight is NOT hex - it is that an event stores IDs and the stoichiometry lives in a static compiled-in table. Hex text is ~2x the size of binary and buys nothing as storage; it is purely a DISPLAY encoding for the dev inspector.

```
struct molecular_event   // 8 bytes, flat binary, fixed width
{
    uint16_t epoch_myr;  // Myr before present / 10 - covers 655 Gyr
    uint8_t  process_id; // index into reaction_table
    uint8_t  outcome;    // fired / marginal / failed / bypassed
    uint16_t yield_q;    // fixed-point, 1/1000
    uint8_t  venue_id;   // vent / pool / pore / lake / subsurface
    uint8_t  flags;
};
```

Two tables in `src/world/chemistry_tables.{hpp,cpp}`, compiled in and NEVER serialised:
- `species_table[]` - id, formula ('HCN'), canonical name ('hydrogen cyanide'), class (feedstock / reductant / monomer / polymer / cofactor / waste). ~35 entries.
- `reaction_table[]` - id, name ('serpentinisation'), reactant ids, product ids, one prose line, owning sub-gate. ~25 entries.

**An event never holds a string.** The hex inspector and any player-facing surface both decode through the SAME table, so names cannot drift from ids and raw bytes can never leak to display. Rendered form:

```
3F 0C 01 4E 20 02 00 00
  3.90 Gya  serpentinisation   FIRED   yield 0.31   venue: alkaline vent
            olivine + H2O -> serpentine + magnetite + H2
```

Budget: ~60 events on a living world, ~10 on a dead one -> **under 500 bytes per body**, comfortably inside the envelope PLANETOLOGY.md already reserves (~120 bytes + a <=64-byte event array).

## Determinism

- **Seven new stage tags** for the RNG sub-streams, plus 2-3 for the S6 sub-gates. Existing tags are tag_accretion 0x51A1, tag_breath 0xB6EA, tag_green 0x67EE, and an inline 0x5A4B at S5. Allocate FRESH constants; PLANETOLOGY.md warns 0x4A71012u is already folded twice in hard_coded_world.cpp.
- **Per-sub-gate hashed sub-streams are load-bearing here**, more than anywhere else in the model: they are what lets a later gate be added or retuned without silently re-rolling every earlier one.
- **The RNA hydrolysis temperature curve MUST be a lookup table**, not exp(). Arrhenius kinetics in a gate path is exactly the portability hazard PLANETOLOGY.md names - exp/log/pow are not bit-identical across compilers, libm versions or fast-math settings. Specify a 16-entry table over 0-160 C, on the precedent of the radiogenic decay already binned at 0.05 Gyr.
- **This is also why the kinetic-network depth was rejected.** Integrating real concentrations over time is nothing BUT exponentials in gate paths; it would need every rate as a lookup, arriving at this design with ~200 free parameters and four calibration bodies.

## Harness impact (tools/verify/planetology_harness.cpp)

**Blast radius is smaller than it looks: three of the four prototype bodies die at S1-S3 and never reach S5, and the fourth (Kepler) is the constrained homeworld the strict floor forces through.**

| Group | Risk |
|---|---|
| R2 four bodies land in stated archetypes | LOW - Kepler must still be Cradle; the floor enforces it |
| R3 B->C joint | unchanged |
| R4 iron/coal antagonism | **AT RISK** - the photosystem fork adds a second, independent iron pathway; re-assert both ends |
| R5 homeworld corridor 100/100 | **AT RISK** - seven new gates the homeworld must clear; acceptance rate will fall, reject-and-reroll absorbs it, but planetology_sweep MUST re-measure per-lean cost so no preference becomes a dead end |
| R7 every knob moves its outcome | new cofactor gates need their own assertions |
| **R12 NEW - the trace** | event sequence is deterministic in (seed, body); and EVERY emitted species/reaction id resolves in the table (no orphan ids). The orphan-id check is the key new invariant, since ids and names are now decoupled |

`abiogenesis_ease` should now bias the WHOLE chain rather than a single draw at S5. No new player knob is proposed - the existing eight preferences already cover the axes, and PLANETOLOGY.md's rule is that a knob must change something a player can read.

## Cut, by the diagnostic test

PLANETOLOGY.md: 'for every generated value, name the decision it changes. Anything that fails is deleted, not tuned.' Cut: **homochirality** (beautiful, names no decision); **nucleobase route** - formamide vs cyanosulfidic vs HCN (three paths, identical output; may survive as flavour naming only); **panspermia** (moves the question, changes nothing); **LUCA's gene set** (invisible downstream); **eukaryogenesis** (borderline - overlaps Boring Billion's 'oxygen present and useless'; revisit only if the Boring Billion outcome proves too rare).

## Residual calls (implementation-time, with recommendations)

1. **Manganese is not currently derived anywhere.** S6b needs it. Recommend a crustal-Mn scalar from metallicity x crustal reworking - cheap, and it reuses S0's one-nebula correlation.
2. **S5f Compartment** - cut if it never fires distinctly from S5e (see above).
3. **Ferrotroph vs Mat World separation** - fold if tuning cannot distinguish them.
4. **Authority propagation:** PLANETOLOGY.md is deliberately NOT edited by this entry. Per the standing rule, a settled design for an open item lives in the item until the work lands, then propagates into the authority doc as part of landing it.

Read PLANETOLOGY.md S5/S6/S8, 'Determinism & cost', 'Known weaknesses' and 'Presentation' in full before promoting.

items.summary: UMBRELLA, DESIGN-OWED 2026-07-28 (Ben session). Reframes generation from four separate mechanisms (planetology chain -> mechanical 6-pass tiles -> Voronoi nations -> focus-table corporations) into ONE continuous simulated history: S1-S4 continents become an actual plate-drift/collision/rift simulation (subsuming BL-051's parked speculative tectonics half) instead of noise/heightmap; the existing S5-S8 biosphere chain (BL-167, extended by BL-209's 7-gate S5/S6) stays the proven template; and a NEW settlement -> industrialisation -> 1900s stage replaces NATION_GENERATION's Voronoi BFS and CORPORATION_GENERATION's authored focus tables with simulated nation/corporate emergence. Extinction-class events (mass extinctions already narrated today, plus new 'historical extinction' analogues - collapses, wars) become BRANCH CHECKPOINTS: the existing world_preferences lean mechanism (BL-167 Round A/B/C) extends to bias which branch fires at each checkpoint, replacing pure reject-and-reroll with reject-reroll-or-branch. The multi-world batch tool (today's planetology_sweep.cpp, sampling seeds) becomes a BRANCH-COMBINATION sweep: it explores lean x checkpoint-branch space, not just seeds, to find which combinations reliably produce good (viable, varied, interesting) worlds - this is the mechanism for tuning target parameters that the user asked for, and it directly answers PLANETOLOGY.md's own named gap ('the pass hands nothing to nation or corporation generation... the largest missing connection'). Deepest-rung choice confirmed 3x by Ben over the narrate-on-top / mechanical-stays / offline-tool-only alternatives (see ben-picks-the-deeper-option memory). This is an UMBRELLA item: each subject doc (TILE_GENERATION continents, NATION_GENERATION/CORPORATION_GENERATION settlement-to-1900s, the checkpoint/branch mechanism itself) needs its own design pass and will likely split into per-doc sub-items once each is settled, same pattern BL-167 followed before it implemented. SETTLED 2026-08-02: all four open items are closed elsewhere — the plate model answered itself in the build (Continents/Drift landed 2026-07-28 as an optional continent_bias INPUT to generate_body_tiles, not a replacement, with CONTINENTS.md as its authority); nations/corporations as output are BL-218/BL-219, settled today; the checkpoint model is BL-217, settled today and deliberately shaped to migrate into BL-208 log; and the cost discipline was honoured in both passes. This is now a PURE UMBRELLA with a three-part closing condition (BL-217/218/219 BUILT, the batch-sweep extension as an execution follow-on not a fourth design item, and authority propagation into the three generation docs at landing). Nothing else may be appended — an umbrella that accretes design is how this became a difficulty-5 blocker. Difficulty 5->2.
items.design:
ARCHITECTURE PROPOSED 2026-07-28, NOT YET SETTLED PER SUBJECT DOC. This entry records the cross-doc shape agreed in session; each subject doc still needs its own design conversation before promotion (see summary).

## Why now

GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's ordering today is four independent mechanisms glued together: planetology (BL-167) runs a real S0-S9 causal chain per body and stops at 'now'; TILE_GENERATION's six-pass pipeline reads planetology's output but is otherwise noise/heightmap/cluster-based, not itself historical; NATION_GENERATION places territory by Voronoi BFS over the tile map, deriving resource profile by summing deposits; CORPORATION_GENERATION places lean specialist holdings by an authored focus table. PLANETOLOGY.md's own 'Known weaknesses' section already names the seam: 'the pass hands nothing to nation or corporation generation... arable share, river connectivity, fossil geography and ore provinces are exactly what should seed Voronoi nation placement and corporate industrial focus... this is the largest missing connection and it is not a small follow-on.' This item is that follow-on, taken to its full depth rather than a patch.

## The new pipeline shape

One continuous simulated history with checkpoints, replacing the current planetology -> tiles -> nations -> corporations handoff:

```
S0 System (unchanged, one campaign-wide roll)
S1-S4 Continents  <- NEW: actual plate drift / collision / rift simulation.
  Terrain is an OUTPUT of this simulated history, not a noise/heightmap pass reading
  static solar parameters. Subsumes BL-051's parked 'speculative orbital-derivation +
  tectonic landforms' half (that item's buildable cosmetic half - band smoothing,
  coastline refinement - is untouched and stays a separate, already-promote-ready sibling pass).
  checkpoint: water-gate / ice-age branch (S4's existing Oven/Snowball/Relict failures,
  reframed as branch points a lean can bias rather than pure reject-reroll)
S5-S8 Biosphere (existing BL-167 chain, extended by BL-209's 7-gate S5/S6 - REUSED AS THE
  PROVEN TEMPLATE, not rewritten)
  checkpoint: mass-extinction branch (already narrated in the eight-line biography today,
  e.g. '252 Mya extinction, recovery took ten million years' - promoted from flavour text
  to an actual branch point)
Settlement -> Industrialisation -> 1900s  <- NEW: replaces NATION_GENERATION's Voronoi BFS
  and CORPORATION_GENERATION's focus tables. Nation territory, political character, and
  corporate industrial focus become OUTPUTS of a simulated settlement/conflict/
  industrialisation history, seeded by the continent and biosphere history above (arable
  share, river connectivity, ore provinces, fossil geography) rather than summed post-hoc
  from tile deposits.
  checkpoint: 'historical extinction' branch (collapse, war, revolution - the historical-
  scale analogue of a mass extinction; also where the post-WW2 industrial grounding open
  item in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md finally gets a mechanism rather than staying an unsettled
  research note)
```

## The checkpoint/branch/lean mechanism

Extends BL-167's already-shipped preferences design (eight axes, each a lean of any/low/mid/high, resolved from the seed via reject-and-reroll, never directly editable - 'if you have preferences you can find them, but really you don't get full customization') rather than inventing a new UI concept. Today a lean narrows a sampling range within ONE round; this generalises it so a lean can also bias WHICH branch fires at a checkpoint (e.g. a 'turbulent' historical lean makes a war-branch more likely at a settlement checkpoint, without ever letting the player type a probability). The existing reject-and-reroll discipline is preserved exactly - a branch is proposed, evaluated against viability floors (the homeworld-viability pattern from BL-167), and rerolled if it fails, never clamped.

## The batch-tuning tool

tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp already measures acceptance rate and per-lean cost by sampling seeds. This generalises the same instrument to sample LEAN x BRANCH-COMBINATION space across the whole pipeline (continents through 1900s), not just seeds within the biosphere chain - the explicit ask being 'generate many worlds, to see what targets are best, and how to tweak the overall strategy.' Two outputs, same as today's sweep: (1) a per-lean/per-branch cost table so a dead-end combination shows up as a number (BL-167's 'no lean is a dead end' rule, extended to branches); (2) the target parameter ranges that go into the eventual constants, the same role today's sweep plays for the homeworld floor.

## What stays fixed

- **The BL-051 sibling-pass architecture convention** (six-pass core stays fixed, extensions land as siblings reading the shared generation_record) - continents-as-history is the biggest sibling pass yet, but the convention itself does not change.
- **The eight-line biography cap and 'diagnostic test' from PLANETOLOGY.md** ('for every generated value, name the decision it changes; anything that fails is deleted, not tuned') - applies to every new stage, not just the biosphere chain.
- **Determinism discipline** - per-stage hashed sub-streams, no std::normal_distribution/uniform_int_distribution, no bare transcendentals in gate paths - all of PLANETOLOGY.md's 'Determinism & cost' section applies unchanged to the new stages.
- **BL-167's homeworld rule** - constrain the inputs (via leans/branches), never clamp the gates.

## What needs its own design pass (not settled here)

1. **TILE_GENERATION.md** - the actual plate-simulation model (how continents drift/collide/rift as a function of S3's tectonic-activity roll already computed by planetology; what replaces the six-pass core's heightmap/noise/cluster approach, or whether it becomes an input to that pipeline rather than a full replacement).
2. **NATION_GENERATION.md + CORPORATION_GENERATION.md** - the settlement/industrialisation/1900s simulation itself: what drives a nation's borders, political character and wealth as OUTPUT rather than Voronoi input; how corporate focus emerges from that history rather than an authored table; how this interacts with the economic premise in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md (saturated substrate, specialist corporations) which must survive the rewrite unchanged in spirit.
3. **The checkpoint/branch data model** - where branch state lives (extends planetology_state? a new per-body/per-nation structure?), and its relationship to BL-208's world-history-log (an append-only narrative substrate already design-owed for a different reason - corp/AI action logging - but a plausible shared storage substrate worth checking before inventing a second one).
4. **Cost.** This is explicitly the deepest option at every branch point Ben was offered (continents: replace vs narrate; nations: simulate vs Voronoi+narrate; multi-world: offline tool vs player-facing vs both-with-branch-checkpoints) - each subject-doc design pass should re-surface the cheaper alternative as a comparison point even though the direction is decided, so the cost is visible rather than assumed.

Read GENERATION_STRATEGY.md in full (ordering, economic premise, open cross-doc items), PLANETOLOGY.md 'Known weaknesses' + 'The homeworld rule' + 'Determinism & cost', and BL-051's parked design before starting any subject-doc pass.

## UPDATE 2026-07-30 - the Settlement stage now has a design authority

`docs/lore/HISTORY.md` (new) is the designed content for this item's `Settlement -> Industrialisation -> 1900s` stage, which this entry named and explicitly left to a later pass. It arrives as a seven-stage causal ladder (agrarian surplus -> the enforceable promise -> fragmentation-with-connectivity -> capital disciplines the sovereign -> energy transition -> the averted rupture -> saturation), promoted into **BL-221** (Stages 0-2, pre-national), **BL-222** (Stages 3-4, industrial) and **BL-223** (Stages 5-6, the premise - design-owed after Ben's reframe). **BL-220** is the timestamp foundation all three need; **BL-224** asserts the non-hegemony invariant Stage 2 claims.

Ben confirmed 2026-07-30 that the ladder is **100% driven, not narrating** - it produces fragmentation, nation count, industrialisation timing and drawdown rather than describing a world already generated. So this entry's open question 2 (NATION_GENERATION + CORPORATION_GENERATION as OUTPUT of a simulated history) is now answered in the direction it proposed, with BL-218 owning the culture/nation half and BL-221/222 the institutional half.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — all four open items are now closed elsewhere. This is a pure umbrella.

Working the design-owed set closed every question this entry left open, three of them today:

| Open item | Where it was closed |
|---|---|
| **1. TILE_GENERATION plate model** | **Already landed 2026-07-28.** The Continents/Drift sibling pass ships as an optional `continent_bias` **input** to `generate_body_tiles`, not a replacement for the six-pass core — the question the item posed ("or whether it becomes an input rather than a full replacement") answered itself in the build. `docs/generation/CONTINENTS.md` is now its authority. |
| **2. NATION + CORPORATION as output** | **BL-218 / BL-219**, settled today. Concrete per-axis character derivation, home-province corporate focus, world-level reject-and-reroll for diversity. |
| **3. Checkpoint/branch data model** | **BL-217**, settled today. Append-only ordered records, deliberately shaped to migrate into BL-208's log as a move rather than a rewrite — which also answers this entry's own "worth checking before inventing a second one". |
| **4. Cost — re-surface the cheaper alternative** | **Honoured in both passes.** BL-218 surfaced Voronoi-plus-narration and rejected it as the lying-figure problem; BL-219 surfaced keeping the authored focus table and replaced it with set-level reroll. |

### What this item IS now

**An umbrella with a closing condition and no design of its own.** It closes when:

1. **BL-217, BL-218 and BL-219 are BUILT** (all three are now `designed`, none built).
2. **The batch-sweep extension** lands — sweeping the lean x branch-combination space. Per
   BL-217's settlement this is an **execution-depth follow-on, not a fourth design item**;
   `tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp` is the model to extend.
3. **Authority propagates** into TILE_GENERATION.md, NATION_GENERATION.md and
   CORPORATION_GENERATION.md — as part of landing the work, per the authority time-slice rule,
   never ahead of it.

Nothing else. If a new design question appears under this pivot it belongs to whichever of
BL-217/218/219 owns that subject, or gets its own id — **not** appended here. An umbrella that
accretes design is how this item became a difficulty-5 blocker in the first place.

**Difficulty 5 -> 2.** Difficulty 5 was the three subject-doc passes, which are now three items
of their own. What remains is a sweep extension and three doc updates.

items.design:
NOT YET SETTLED. Scope and open questions, to be resolved in its own design pass (per the doc-by-doc sign-off pattern this session used for BL-210):

## What already exists to build on

- **The developer-facing ledger is fully designed** (GENERATION_LEDGER.md): a per-tile derivation breadcrumb (height -> ocean -> band/moisture -> composition -> landform -> deposits) and per-body summaries (composition/landform histograms, key thresholds, profile echo), regenerated on demand from `generation_record` rather than persisted.
- **Planetology's eight-line biography** (PLANETOLOGY.md 'Presentation') is the textual convention this ledger should extend, not replace: dated lines, two columns (what happened / what it left behind), asymmetric length (a Cradle gets eight lines, a dead world gets three), homeworld-relative units. `continents.hpp`'s `history_event` struct already reuses this exact shape (chain_stage::engine lines) — this item's job is giving those lines, and the ones Nations/Corporations will eventually emit, an actual place to be READ.
- **MENU.md's History slot is already settled as the destination** — gated by exploration (BL-067's survey fog), a distinct informational set from a live event log, gives 'post-generation advisory' on resource/workforce state.

## What needs deciding

1. **Scope for THIS pass vs. later passes.** BL-210 has so far only landed Continents/Drift; Biosphere (Planetology) already has its full biography; Nations/Corporations don't exist yet as causal-consequence output. Does the History slot ship incrementally (biosphere biography first, since it's already fully built and just needs a UI home) or wait for the whole BL-210 chain?
2. **One long narrative per body, or per-nation/per-corp sub-views once those land?** The existing biography is per-body. Once Nations/Corporations become oral-history outputs (BL-210's remaining scope), does History gain a nation tab, a corp tab, or does everything stay nested under its body?
2b. **Exploration-gating interaction.** A body's Continents/Drift and Biosphere history should probably be visible once surveyed (matches the existing 'Air must show full history at campaign start' exception PLANETOLOGY.md already carries for the homeworld) — but Nations/Corporations history may need its own gate (DISCOVERY.md's activity fog?) since it is about *current* political/economic actors, not dead geology.
3. **Shared content builder or a new one?** GENERATION_LEDGER.md already commits the per-tile breadcrumb to a shared builder (ledger panel / hover card / Selection element all call it, per SELECTION.md). Should the biography text follow the same shared-builder discipline (so a future 'why does this nation have this ideology' hover reuses the same text as the History panel), or is prose long-form enough that it only ever renders in one place?
4. **Render surface.** `src/ui/charts.{hpp,cpp}` already exists for bar-chart-style summaries (reused across the Planetology wizard and tile-selection deposit graphs) — the History slot's per-body summaries should reuse it rather than inventing new chart code. The dated-line biography itself is plain text, so no new charting need there.

Read GENERATION_LEDGER.md in full (especially § Open items 'Player-facing variant') and MENU.md's History slot entry before starting this design pass.

## UPDATE 2026-07-30

`docs/lore/HISTORY.md` § Open questions asks how much of its stage ladder surfaces to the player - a codex, generated history lines only, or ambient quest flavour. **Answered by this item already existing:** the first slice shipped in b90ba10 (nav slot 9 "History", the "Generation History" section rendering `planetology_state::history` as dated two-column text), so the ladder's lines join the biography that is already there. No codex, no second surface.

Two consequences for this item: (1) it must render **historical** dates as well as deep-time ones, which is **BL-220**'s timestamp change; (2) the biography grows by ~7 lines from BL-221/222/223, so PLANETOLOGY.md's eight-line summary cap now needs the drill-down BL-217 assumes rather than a flat list.
