items.progress_note: LANDED 2026-07-28 (Batch Delivery with BL-211). Design settled: (1) aggregation rule = one heaviest event per (nation, tick), severity-ranked by kind (idled/demolished highest, built/recipe_switch/resumed mid, road/workforce/survey lowest), silent ticks produce no post (ledgers-start-closed precedent); (2) voice source = the nation itself (entity_id posted to chat, not the corp) with generic first-person phrasing per event kind, NOT yet keyed by nation ideology/politics (left as a future increment, noted in code); (3) underlying corp-level detail is DROPPED, not kept private-but-viewable anywhere — the old per-corp/per-building Public text was actually a standing violation of DISCOVERY.md's competitor-visibility rule (it leaked rival internals), so removing it is a bugfix as much as a feature; (4) confirmed disjoint from BL-211 (comms = live present-tense, History = retrospective); (5) Beliefs dependency confirmed non-blocking, uses existing nation_component::politics-less generic phrasing for now. Implementation: src/core/app.cpp's step_economy agency-event loop rewritten to aggregate per corporation_component::home_nation and post via ui::chat_post with the nation's entity_id; the epoch line now counts nations, not corporations. src/ui/chat_panel.{hpp,cpp} gained speaker_name/speaker_colour (try world::nations first, fall back to world::corporations) so Public messages render with the nation's name and ui::palette::nation_colour while Counsel channels (BL-207, still corp-authored, unchanged) keep working. Verified visually (scripts/verify/history_ledger_and_comms.lua) — 'd0  21 nations on the public channel.' renders correctly. Regression-checked: determinism_harness, world_audit, continents_harness all still PASS (this item touches UI/app.cpp only, no world/* logic). NOT DONE: nation-ideology-flavoured phrasing (open question 2 in the design), and no golden yet for the new capture (capture-only).
items.summary: DESIGN-OWED 2026-07-28 (Ben session, playtest follow-up). Ben's call: 'anonymise a lot of the chat log (only nations speak, and they pretend it is their own voice)' — the Public comms channel should never show an individual corporation's message; every public post is attributed to a NATION, voiced in the first person, standing in for whatever its registered corporations actually did. This is the EXACT SHAPE of the already-settled competitor-visibility rule (DISCOVERY.md: 'Rival internals are private... market supply/demand aggregates and prices are public — the deliberate signal. The player reasons over public signals, not handed over'), extended from the market channel to the comms channel. Today's Public channel opens with a placeholder epoch line only (BL-205, app.cpp:672-675: '<N> corporations on the public channel') — the real per-corp message generation is the corp_ai/persona-pack layer (BL-202/BL-207, persona::pack's in-voice claim/explanation strings), which currently has no notion of a nation-level mouthpiece at all. SETTLED 2026-08-02: aggregation is MOST-CONSEQUENTIAL-WINS, at most one statement per nation per tick, ranked off BL-202 existing scored-utility layer with a corp-id tie-break — not a digest, which at 43 nations is a wall of text and destroys the voice. Silence is the normal case. The nation becomes a persona WRAPPING the corp personas, and the item does NOT wait on BL-218: it reads ideology/expansionism rather than generating them, so it works against today random draw and improves automatically when BL-218 makes them a consequence. Corp chatter is KEPT as the private layer (own corps visible, rivals never — BL-068), giving comms the same private-detail/public-aggregate structure as markets. History Ledger stays DISJOINT — putting live statements there would re-create exactly the problem NR-020 is trying to remove. Free-text/LLM voice is Stage C, not this.
items.design:
NOT YET SETTLED. Open questions for its own design pass:

## The pattern this extends

DISCOVERY.md already settled the general shape: private detail (rival production/stockpiles) stays hidden; a public AGGREGATE signal (market prices/supply-demand) is what the player actually reasons over. This item is that same rule applied to comms instead of markets: corp-level chatter (whatever corp_ai/persona_pack generates per-corp today) becomes the PRIVATE layer; a nation-level statement is the only thing that ever reaches the Public channel, and it is phrased as if the nation itself is speaking, not reporting on a corporation.

## What needs deciding

1. **Aggregation rule.** When multiple corporations registered in the same nation act in a way that would generate a persona message, how does that collapse into ONE national statement? Loudest/most consequential action wins? A running digest? Does a quiet tick produce no national message at all (silence is fine — 'ledgers-start-closed' convention already used elsewhere)?
2. **Voice source.** `persona::pack` already produces in-voice claim/explanation strings (<=140 chars) per persona — is a NATION now a persona (its `ideology`/`expansionism`/`economic_focus` from NATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4 become the voice), replacing or wrapping the corp-level persona? Note NATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4's ideology/expansionism are currently a random draw, not a consequence (the same gap BL-210's Nations rewrite is targeting) — this item may want to wait on that, or may motivate doing it sooner.
3. **Does the underlying corp-level chatter still exist anywhere?** Fully deleted, or does it become the 'private' layer visible only to the corp's own player/rival-audit surfaces (symmetric with market private/public split)? If kept, where does a curious player ever see it (a corp dossier? nothing at all, matching 'rival internals are private... never appear')?
4. **Interaction with the History Ledger (BL-211).** A nation's public voice is a live, ongoing signal; the History Ledger is retrospective generation record. Likely disjoint surfaces (comms = present-tense play, History = how-we-got-here), but worth confirming they don't want to be the same panel.
5. **Beliefs dependency.** Out of scope here per this session's standing note ([[ben-generation-consequences-not-simulation]]) — Beliefs (Fable's) may eventually flavour a nation's voice, but this item should not block on it; a nation's voice can start from the existing ideology/expansionism/economic_focus attributes alone.

Read DISCOVERY.md in full (especially the competitor-visibility rule this generalises), corp_ai.hpp/persona_pack.hpp (the existing per-corp voice mechanism), and NATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4 (today's ideology/expansionism draw) before starting this design pass.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the five questions

### 1. Aggregation — the most consequential action wins, at most one statement per nation per tick

Not a digest. A digest produces a paragraph per nation per tick, which at 43 nations is a wall
of text nobody reads, and it destroys the thing the item is for: a *statement* has a voice, a
summary does not.

**Silence is the normal case and needs no apology.** Most ticks, most nations do nothing worth
saying. That matches the ledgers-start-closed convention the item cites and it is what makes a
statement mean something when one arrives — a channel that speaks every tick is noise with
personality.

"Most consequential" needs a deterministic ordering, and it has one for free: the corp AI's
scored-utility layer (BL-202) already ranks actions. Take the highest-magnitude action among the
nation's corporations that tick, with an explicit tie-break on corporation id.

### 2. Voice source — the nation becomes a persona that WRAPS the corp personas

Not a replacement. The corp-level persona machinery keeps working and keeps generating; the
national voice is a layer over it that speaks about the aggregate.

**On the ideology dependency — this item does NOT wait on BL-218.** NATION_GENERATION Pass 4's
ideology/expansionism are a random draw today, and BL-218 is what makes them a consequence of
settlement history. But this item *reads* those fields; it does not generate them. So it works
now against a random draw and **improves automatically** when BL-218 lands, with no rework —
the voice gets better because its input got truer.

That is the right relationship and worth stating, because the item wondered whether to wait.
Waiting would buy nothing: the consuming code is identical either way.

### 3. Corp-level chatter — KEPT, as the private layer

Deleted would throw away working machinery and break the symmetry the item is built on.

- **Your own corporations' chatter: visible to you.** It is your own internals.
- **Rival corporations' chatter: never visible.** BL-068 settles that rival internals are
  private, and chatter is internals.
- **The Public channel carries only national statements.**

So the structure is exactly the market's: private detail, public aggregate. The player sees
their own corps speak, hears nations speak, and never overhears a rival — which is the same
rule they already understand from prices.

### 4. History Ledger — DISJOINT. Confirmed, not merged.

Comms is present-tense play; the History Ledger is how the world came to be. They share nothing
but a text rendering.

Worth confirming rather than assuming, because NR-020 is currently proposing the History ledger
lose its current-state view for precisely this reason — a ledger about the past should not
accumulate present-tense surfaces. Putting live national statements there would re-create the
problem NR-020 is trying to remove.

### 5. Beliefs — out of scope, unchanged

Already settled by the standing note. The voice starts from ideology / expansionism /
economic_focus alone.

### Not in scope

Any free-text or LLM-generated voice — that is Stage C (AI_OPPONENT.md §2 Area C), a separate
tier that BL-205's channel surface is the medium for. This item is templated statements in a
national voice, nothing more.

items.title: Drill-through as a common concept - one progressive-disclosure idiom every dense surface obeys, so a compact read is the default and depth is asked for
items.summary: Raised by Ben on seeing the BL-211 History ledger land (2026-07-29): 'This is fantastic... compact and readable. HOWEVER, for many people it would be information overload.' The History ledger is the case in point - three round tabs over ten stage accordions, each holding two to four charts plus two paragraphs of physics. It is legible because Ben already read that chain once in the wizard; a player who has not is handed a wall. The ask is NOT to cut the depth. It is to make drill-through a CONCEPT the whole UI shares - a compact top layer everywhere, depth reached by an explicit uniform gesture - rather than a per-surface decision each ledger re-invents.

items.title: Render-precision audit - walk every UI element and confirm text wraps rather than clips, at the smallest supported display
items.summary: Raised by Ben 2026-07-29 alongside BL-211: 'the other mistake is that text does not wrap fully. We need to go through UI elements and double check things render with precision, leaving text to wrap on smaller monitors.' Concrete instances found while building the History ledger: chart TITLES clip mid-word in the fold-out column ('Metals (homeworld endowment, 1.0 ='); chart LEGEND rows clip their value ('Agricultural Produce 0'); the stage accordion header clipped its question until it was shortened to the stage name; the biography's consequence lines clipped until switched to TextWrapped. Each was fixed or dodged locally - this item is the systematic pass.

items.title: Shell re-plan - move the comms log to the bottom-left corner and give the freed centre-right band back to pinned items
items.summary: Raised by Ben 2026-07-29, immediately after BL-213 put the Selection band along the bottom: 'it could be worth moving the chat log to the bottom left corner. This will make it look a bit better with our selection element / menu both wanting that space. We can refactor the pinned items back to the centre right space.' Two moves in one: comms leaves the right chrome column for the bottom-left, and the band it vacates (right edge, between the time panel and the minimap) returns to PINNED ITEMS - the affordance the Explorer placeholder reserved before the comms log replaced it on 2026-07-26.
items.design:
## BL-216 — Shell re-plan: comms to the bottom band, pinned items to the freed centre-right

**Status: designed, 2026-07-30.** Ben settled the two blocking questions (comms gets its own rect
left of the Selection band; pinned items are built for real). Everything below is settled on his
behalf and is authoritative for implementation. The item's original sequencing note (behind
BL-215/BL-214) is **overridden** — Ben authorised this now.

---

### 1. The shape

The bottom of the screen becomes **one strip with two tiles**, sandwiched as before between the
full-height shell column and the full-height right chrome column:

```
┌──────────┬─────┬──────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
│ Profile  │     │           Header             │  Time panel  │
├──────────┤     ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Nav rail │Fold-│                              │              │
│ (icons)  │out  │       Primary canvas         │ PINNED ITEMS │
│ ▢ ▢ ▦ …  │col  │                              │ (watch list) │
│          │(full│                              ├──────────────┤
│          │hght)├────────┬─────────────────────┤   Minimap    │
│          │     │ COMMS  │  SELECTION BAND     │  [lens bar]  │
└──────────┴─────┴────────┴─────────────────────┴──────────────┘
```

The **fold-out ledger column is untouched** — it still runs `profile_panel_height → disp.y`, so the
BL-117 one-question-per-view splits keep the vertical budget they were sized against. Comms starts
at `x = shell_column_width(disp.x)`, so column and dock are horizontally disjoint; nothing occludes
anything.

---

### 2. Rect algebra — one owner

Recon hazard #1 is that `disp.x - margin - mm_w` is re-derived **five times** in `app.cpp`
(`:2291`, `:2414`, `:2509`, `:2585`, `:2645`) with no owning function. Adding a fourth region on top
of that guarantees drift. So the foundation of this item is a new module.

**`src/ui/shell_metrics.{hpp,cpp}`** — the single home of the shell's rect algebra. It *consumes*
`shell_column_width` / `foldout_column_rect` (which stay in `foldout_column.hpp`) and does not
duplicate them.

```cpp
namespace ui {

struct shell_rect { float x, y, w, h; };

inline constexpr float shell_margin             = 8.0f;   // the screen gutter app.cpp uses
inline constexpr float comms_rail_width         = nav_pane_width;  // 56 — the shell's collapsed-strip idiom
inline constexpr float comms_dock_min_width     = 300.0f;
inline constexpr float comms_dock_max_width     = 440.0f;
inline constexpr float comms_dock_band_reserve  = 560.0f; // band width the dock must leave behind to dock

enum class comms_dock_mode { docked, railed };

float       right_chrome_width(ImVec2 disp);   // max(336, 0.28 * min(disp.x, disp.y))  == mm_w
float       right_chrome_left (ImVec2 disp);   // disp.x - shell_margin - right_chrome_width(disp)
shell_rect  minimap_rect      (ImVec2 disp);
float       bottom_band_budget(ImVec2 disp);   // max(0, right_chrome_left - shell_column_width)

comms_dock_mode comms_dock_mode_for(ImVec2 disp);
shell_rect  comms_dock_rect     (ImVec2 disp);          // docked: full panel; railed: 56px strip
shell_rect  comms_peek_rect     (ImVec2 disp);          // railed-mode overlay, over the band
shell_rect  selection_band_rect (ImVec2 disp);
shell_rect  pinned_panel_rect   (ImVec2 disp, float time_h);

} // namespace ui
```

**Comms dock width:**

```
budget = bottom_band_budget(disp)
wanted = clamp(round(0.32f * budget), comms_dock_min_width, comms_dock_max_width)
dock_w = (wanted <= budget - comms_dock_band_reserve) ? wanted
       : (budget >= comms_rail_width ? comms_rail_width : 0.0f)
```

All widths are rounded to whole pixels, exactly as `shell_column_width` already does, so every
region edge lands on a pixel boundary.

**Selection band:** `x = shell_column_width(disp.x) + dock_w`, `w = max(0, budget - dock_w)`,
`y = disp.y - selection_band_height`, `h = selection_band_height` (340, **unchanged**).
There is **no gap** between the dock and the band — the band is already flush against the shell
column and the right chrome, and introducing the shell's only gutter here would read as a mistake.

**Resolved, at every supported size:**

| Display | `mm_w` | `right` | `W` | budget | mode | dock_w | band.w | (band today) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1280 × 720  | 336   | 936  | 380 | 556  | **railed** | 56  | **500**  | 556 |
| 1600 × 900  | 336   | 1256 | 380 | 876  | docked | 300 | 576  | 876 |
| 1720 × 1080 | 336   | 1376 | 380 | 996  | docked | 319 | 677  | 996 |
| 1920 × 1080 | 336   | 1576 | 384 | 1192 | docked | 381 | 811  | 1192 |
| 2560 × 1440 | 403.2 | 2149 | 460 | 1689 | docked | 440 | 1249 | 1689 |

The dock threshold falls at **≈1584 px display width** — the 1600×900 preset and up dock; 1280×720
rails. At the 640×480 settings floor `budget` clamps to 0, `dock_w` to 0 and `band.w` to 0: the same
fail-soft the band already has, no new failure mode.

---

### 3. The smallest supported display — measured, not clamped

**1280 × 720 has 556 px for the whole bottom band** (1280 − 380 shell column − 344 right chrome).
There is no honest width assignment that seats a readable comms panel *and* the BL-213 tile
three-column layout in 556 px. Rather than clamp comms to a sliver or pretend, the layout states
the threshold and degrades into an idiom the shell already owns:

- **Railed mode.** The dock renders as a **56 px full-band-height rail** at `x = W` — the same width
  as `nav_pane_width`, so it reads as a second vertical rail rhyming with the nav rail across the
  bottom-left corner. It carries the `icons::pin`-family comms glyph, an **unread badge**, and the
  newest speaker's identity swatch. Container policy: **container 8** (icon-only, tooltip wraps).
- **Peek.** Clicking the rail toggles `ui_state::comms_peek`, drawing the full comms panel at
  `comms_peek_rect` — the band's rect, `x = band.x`, `w = min(comms_dock_max_width, band.w)` —
  **after** the band in draw order, so it wins z-order. Re-clicking the rail closes it (the standing
  toggle rule: its active state is visible, so re-click undoes). Esc also closes it.
- **Cost, stated:** at 1280 the band goes 556 → 500 px (≈10%). The tile layout's quarters go
  139 → 125 and its centre 262 → 234. Tight, and already tight; BL-215 is the item that makes narrow
  hosts render correctly, and it inherits this width as its target.

**The docked/railed choice is purely derived from `disp`.** There is no player collapse toggle:
the band's rect stays a pure function of display size, with no hidden state to get stuck in.
`comms_peek` is the only comms state, and it is forced `false` every frame in docked mode.

---

### 4. Comms — internal re-layout for the new host

At 1720×1080 comms goes **336 × 698 → 319 × 340**: essentially the same width, half the rows. The
problem is *vertical*, so every change buys rows. All of it stays inside the existing
wrap + vertical-scroll policy — no measured boxes, no new text policy.

1. **Fold the label into the control row.** The standalone `TextDisabled("COMMS")` + `Separator`
   (`chat_panel.cpp:73-74`) goes; `COMMS` becomes a leading dim label on the channel row. *Buys a
   text line + a separator.*
2. **One-line message form.** Replace the two-line stanza (`TextWrapped` day+speaker, then
   `Indent()` + `TextWrapped(body)` + `Unindent()`, `:152-158`) with a **single wrapped paragraph**:
   dim `d%d `, then the speaker in its identity colour, then `": "` — each via `SameLine(0.0f, 0.0f)`
   — then `TextWrapped(body)`. System lines (`from == null_entity`) stay one dim wrapped line.
   *Buys ~40% of rows.*
3. **Channel selector, not a tab chain.** The `SameLine` chain of `SmallButton`s (`:77-99`) has **no
   overflow handling** and clips silently — a real defect the narrower dock would expose. Replace it
   with a single-row `ImGui::BeginCombo` over `chat.channels` plus the `"+"` button on the same line.
   A channel selector is a **cross-cutting selector** and therefore explicitly exempt from the toggle
   rule, so this costs no rule complexity. *Buys unbounded channel count in one fixed row.*
4. **Cap the group popup.** `SetNextWindowSizeConstraints({220,0},{320,260})` and put the per-corp
   checkbox list (`:107-114`) inside `BeginChild("##grp_members", {0.0f, 160.0f})` so it scrolls
   instead of growing unbounded upward from a bottom-anchored popup.
5. **Floor guard.** Keep `if (height <= 0.0f) return;` and add `if (height < 120.0f) return;` — below
   that ImGui clamps the log child's negative height to 4 px and pushes the input row out of the
   window. Defensive only (height is always 340 today).
6. **Unread counters.** `chat_state` gains `int posted_total = 0;` (incremented in `chat_post`) and
   `int seen_total = 0;` (set to `posted_total` on every frame the panel *body* draws, docked or
   peeked). Unread = `max(0, posted_total - seen_total)`, displayed on the rail badge, capped `9+`.
   Counters rather than `messages.size()` because the 300-line ring saturates.
7. **New entry point** in `chat_panel.hpp`:
   `void draw_chat_rail(const world&, const chat_state&, ui_state&, float x, float y, float w, float h);`
   `draw_chat_panel`'s signature is **unchanged** (the 4-float convention); only its doc comment
   changes — `chat_panel.hpp:61-73` currently hard-codes "right shell band … below the time column,
   above the minimap" and "@param x Left edge (aligned with the minimap)".

---

### 5. Pinned items — a real surface

The freed centre-right slot is **exactly** the rect comms vacates:
`{right_chrome_left(disp), shell_margin + time_h + shell_margin, right_chrome_width(disp),
minimap_rect(disp).y - shell_margin - y}` — 336 × ~698 @1720×1080, 336 × ~338 @1280×720.

**The minimap does not move**, and the right column's vertical budget keeps today's two-way elastic
split: time panel (content-derived `time_h`) on top, **pins take the whole residual**, minimap +
lens bar locked bottom-right (`mm_h = 0.75 · mm_w`). The feared three-way split never happens —
comms *leaves* as pins *arrive*. It is a swap, not an addition.

#### What a pin is

A **watch card**: a title row (`draw_selection_icon` kind glyph, entity name, then right-aligned
`[>]` go-to and `[x]` unpin) over the shared **`entity_summary`** stat block for that entity —
`draw_body_summary` / `draw_tile_summary` / `draw_building_summary` / `draw_market_summary` /
`draw_unit_summary` / `draw_nation_summary` / `draw_corporation_summary`. That covers every
`selection_kind` except `none`, so no kind is unpinnable.

**It is deliberately not the Selection band's action content.** Those builders
(`draw_selection_content`, `draw_tile_selection`, `draw_building_selection`, `draw_selection_action`,
`draw_selection_facts`) are entity-*implicit* — every one reads `ui.selected_entity` — and they
mutate singletons: `card_resource_page` is **bound by reference** and paged in place,
`card_stack` is a single drill stack, `show_build_ledger` + `construction.pending_*` are single
per-frame slots. Hosting them twice needs entity threading through five functions plus per-host
keying of three singletons. `entity_summary` is already entity-parameterised, already the sanctioned
second-host path (`draw_hover_card` uses it), already **mandated** by LAYOUT.md § Ledger family
conventions for shared per-entity stat blocks, contains exactly one widget id, writes no `ui_state`
and tolerates stale ids.

**Pins are a watch list, not a second action surface.** Acting on a pin is one click away: clicking
it makes it the selection and the band shows the full action content. In BL-214's terms the pin sits
at the shallow rung and the band at the deep one; BL-214 may re-level it, and this is the pre-
registration for that.

**ID collision:** two market pins would share `BeginTable("market_summary", …)`. Every pin card is
wrapped in `ImGui::PushID(static_cast<int>(entity))` / `PopID()`. That is the whole fix.

#### Rules

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Cap** | `ui::pinned_items_max = 6`. Panel scrolls when cards exceed the height. |
| **Cap reached** | The band's pin button renders **disabled** with tooltip *"Pin list full (6) - unpin one first."* — never a silent drop. |
| **Order** | Append at the end; never reorder. A watch list is learned by position. |
| **Persistence** | **Session-local, not serialised** — matching `chat_state` and every other `ui_state` field. Rides the BL-202/BL-205-slice-2 landing when commands become world state. |
| **Destroyed entity** | Pruned **silently** by `ui::prune_pins(w, ui)` at the top of `draw_pinned_panel` (drops any id where `selection_kind_of(w,id) == none`). SELECTION.md already says "treat a missing id as no selection". |
| **Click a pin** | **Single-click** the card body → `ui.selected_entity = id; ui.selection_hidden_for = null_entity;` (band opens on it). **Double-click** → `focus_on_entity(w, ui, id)`. The `[>]` button does the double-click. This is SELECTION.md's uniform click model, extended — not a new gesture. |
| **Empty state** | Dim wrapped text: *"No pinned items. Use the [pin] button on the Selection band to watch an entity here."* An unexplained empty first-class surface was the Explorer's original sin. |
| **Rail slot** | **None.** Fixed shell chrome, not a ledger — absent from `close_all_panels` / `any_panel_open`, same as comms and the band. |

#### Adding a pin

A `[pin]` button in the Selection band header's right-aligned cluster, immediately **left** of
`[>]` and `[x]`. There are three structurally identical header copies today; adding a fourth button
to each would guarantee drift, so **factor the cluster once**:

```cpp
// selection_panel.hpp
/// Right-aligned chrome cluster for the Selection band header: [pin] [>] [x].
/// Measures its own offset from @p bar_w. Close sets ui.selection_hidden_for.
void draw_selection_header_buttons(world& w, ui_state& ui, entity_id id,
                                   float bar_w, bool show_goto);
```

- `selection_panel.cpp:1209-1218` (generic header) → `draw_selection_header_buttons(w, ui, ui.selected_entity, bar_w, /*show_goto=*/true);`
- `selection_panel.cpp:599-604` (tile header) → `draw_selection_header_buttons(w, ui, sel, avail, /*show_goto=*/false);` (a tile has no go-to today and keeps none)
- `selection_card.cpp:36-62` (drill header) → **unchanged**. A drill frame is not pinnable; pin its root tile.

The pin button is a **toggle**: when `is_pinned(ui, id)` it renders filled in `palette::pinned`
(`IM_COL32(255,200,90,255)` — defined for the Explorer and unused ever since; this is the slot it
was made for) with tooltip *"Unpin"*, and re-clicking unpins. That is mandatory under the standing
toggle rule.

#### New module

```cpp
// src/ui/pins.hpp
namespace ui {
inline constexpr int pinned_items_max = 6;

bool is_pinned  (const ui_state& ui, entity_id e);
bool toggle_pin (ui_state& ui, entity_id e);          ///< true if now pinned; no-op + false when full
void prune_pins (const world& w, ui_state& ui);
void draw_pinned_panel(const world& w, ui_state& ui, float x, float y, float width, float height);
}
```

`ui_state` gains `std::vector<entity_id> pinned_entities;` and `bool comms_peek = false;`.
`icons.{hpp,cpp}` gains `void pin(ImDrawList* dl, ImVec2 centre, float r, ImU32 colour);` — a
pushpin (circular head + tapering stem), catalogued in `docs/ui/ICONS.md`.

**Canvas amber highlight is out of scope.** `ui::resolve_highlight(selected, hovered, pinned)`
already exists and `highlight::pinned` is still unwired on the canvases; wiring it is the natural
immediate follow-on (three canvas files, outside this item's scope) and should be filed as such.

---

### 6. Draw order, input, and Esc

In `app::render()`:

1. …existing chrome…
2. **Pinned panel** at `pinned_panel_rect(disp, time_h)` — replaces the `exp_*` block at
   `app.cpp:2591-2599` in place.
3. **Comms** at `comms_dock_rect(disp)`: docked → `draw_chat_panel`; railed → `draw_chat_rail`.
   Drawn **before** the band.
4. **Selection band** at `selection_band_rect(disp)`.
5. **Comms peek** at `comms_peek_rect(disp)` — only when railed **and** `ui.comms_peek`. Drawn
   **after** the band so it wins z-order.

No manual canvas hit-test is needed: every new region is a real ImGui window, so `io.WantCaptureMouse`
already gates `primary_input` (only the background-draw-list minimap needs its explicit rect test,
and that is unchanged).

**Esc ladder** (`app.cpp:1795-1804`) gains one rung, after the system menu and before the drill stack:

```
confirm_exit_pending → show_system_menu → comms_peek → pop card_stack → hide selection → open system menu
```

---

### 7. Container vocabulary — nine, still

Neither new surface invents a tenth container.

- **Comms dock** and **Pinned items panel** are instances of **container 1** — fixed-width column,
  *wrap to inner width*, *vertical scroll*. LAYOUT.md's row 1 is renamed from
  "Fold-out ledger column" to **"Fixed shell column / dock"**, listing its three instances
  (fold-out ledger column, comms dock, pinned items panel).
- **Comms rail** is an instance of **container 8** (nav rail — icon-only, tooltips wrap).

Declaring the policy up front means BL-215's audit inherits two compliant surfaces rather than two
new offenders.

---

### 8. Stale artefacts cleared in passing

- `app.cpp:2593-2596` — `exp_x/exp_y/exp_w/exp_h` (Explorer naming for comms) renamed `comms_*`.
- `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md:20-21` — the canvas does **not** "shrink vertically to clear the Selection
  band"; it draws full-window at `{0,0}, disp` and the band overlays it. Corrected.
- `foldout_column.cpp:19` and `LAYOUT.md:52` — "~410 px at 1920" is arithmetically wrong
  (`0.20 · 1920 = 384`). Corrected in both.
- `ledger_chrome.cpp`'s `ledger_window_spawn` / `ledger_window_size` are confirmed caller-less;
  their deletion belongs to its own cleanup, not here.

---

### 9. Documentation owed

| Doc | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md` | New ASCII diagram; new **§ Comms dock — bottom band, left** and **§ Pinned items — right column, middle**; § Comms log relocated; container row 1 renamed + instances listed; the two stale claims fixed. |
| `docs/ui/CHAT.md` | Placement rewritten (bottom band, left); the docked/railed rungs + the ≈1584 px threshold; the one-line message form; the channel combo; unread counters. |
| **`docs/ui/PINS.md`** (new) | The pinned-items spec: what a pin is, the `entity_summary` depth, cap, order, persistence, pruning, click model, empty state, its relation to BL-214's disclosure ladder. |
| `docs/ui/EXPLORER.md` | Keep the supersession record; add one line that pinning **has** returned, designed fresh under BL-216 → `PINS.md`, as predicted. |
| `docs/ui/SELECTION.md` | The band's new rect (`x` moves right by `dock_w`); the `[pin]` button in the header cluster; the factored `draw_selection_header_buttons`; drill frames not pinnable. |
| `docs/ui/ICONS.md` | The `pin` glyph. |
| `docs/ui/MINIMAP.md` | One line: the minimap does not move; the right column's split is time / pins / minimap. |

---

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

1. **Comms shares the band's top edge and height** (`disp.y − 340`, height 340), making the screen
   bottom one strip of two tiles, with **zero gap** between them (the shell is otherwise flush).
2. **Comms width = `clamp(round(0.32 · budget), 300, 440)`**, subject to a band-first reserve of
   **560 px**; below that it falls to a **56 px rail** (= `nav_pane_width`).
3. **1280 × 720 rails.** Docking starts at ≈1584 px wide (the 1600×900 preset). The band loses 56 px
   at 1280 (556 → 500) — an accepted, stated cost, not a hidden one.
4. **Railed comms stays reachable** via a peek overlay over the band, toggled by the rail and closed
   by Esc — `ui_state::comms_peek` is the only comms state added.
5. **Docked vs railed is derived from `disp`, never from player state.** No collapse toggle in v1.
6. **The fold-out column keeps its full height**, untouched, per Ben's fixed call.
7. **A pinned item renders the `entity_summary` block, not the band's action content** — the depth
   that is already re-hostable; `PushID(entity)` is the entire collision fix.
8. **`pinned_items_max = 6`**, appended order, panel scrolls; a full list disables the pin button
   with a reason.
9. **Pins are session-local, not serialised.**
10. **A destroyed pinned entity is pruned silently.**
11. **Single-click a pin selects; double-click navigates** — SELECTION.md's existing click model.
12. **The minimap does not move**; the right column keeps its two-way elastic split with pins as the
    residual.
13. **Comms re-lays out for rows, not width:** label folded into the control row, one-line message
    form, channel **combo** replacing the clipping tab chain, size-capped group popup.
14. **The header button cluster is factored once** (`draw_selection_header_buttons`) rather than the
    pin being added in three places.
15. **A new `shell_metrics` module owns the shell rect algebra**, retiring the five hand-rolled
    right-edge derivations — done first, as a no-visual-change foundation.
16. **No new container kind.** Both surfaces are declared instances of containers 1 and 8.
17. **Canvas amber (`highlight::pinned`) wiring is out of scope**, named as the immediate follow-on.

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

Ben delegated these calls for the ultracode session and was unavailable; each is recorded here so it can be reviewed or overturned.

**Q. Where exactly does the comms rect sit, and what is its width/height derivation?**

- **Decision:** Comms occupies the LEFT of the existing bottom band strip: x = ui::shell_column_width(disp.x), y = disp.y - ui::selection_band_height, height = selection_band_height (340, unchanged). Width is derived by a new ui::comms_dock_rect() in a new src/ui/shell_metrics.{hpp,cpp}: budget = max(0, right_chrome_left(disp) - shell_column_width(disp.x)); wanted = clamp(round(0.32*budget), comms_dock_min_width=300, comms_dock_max_width=440); dock_w = (wanted <= budget - comms_dock_band_reserve=560) ? wanted : (budget >= comms_rail_width ? comms_rail_width : 0). No gap between comms and the band (0 px), matching the band's existing flush idiom against the shell column and right chrome.
- **Why:** Sharing the band's top edge and height makes the bottom of the screen ONE strip with two tiles rather than a new horizontal level — the cheapest thing to learn. The width is a residual with a floor/ceiling so it scales with the display instead of being a magic constant, exactly as shell_column_width already does. Zero gap because introducing one here would be the only gap in a shell that is otherwise flush.

**Q. What does comms do at the smallest supported display (1280x720)?**

- **Decision:** It RAILS. At 1280x720 budget=556 and 556-560 < 300, so dock_w falls to comms_rail_width (56 px, defined as == ui::nav_pane_width). The rail is a full-band-height glyph strip at x = W with a comms icon and an unread badge; clicking it toggles ui_state::comms_peek, which draws the full comms panel as an OVERLAY over the band rect (drawn after the band, so it wins z-order), dismissed by re-clicking the rail or Esc. Docking begins at ~1584 px display width, i.e. the 1600x900 preset and up.
- **Why:** Measured, not clamped: 1280 - 380 (shell column) - 344 (right chrome) leaves 556 px for the whole bottom band; there is no honest way to seat a readable comms panel AND the BL-213 tile three-column layout in 556 px. Rather than pretend, the layout states the threshold and degrades to the shell's existing collapsed-strip idiom (the nav rail), so the content stays one click away at every resolution instead of vanishing. The rail costs the band 56 px at 1280 (556 -> 500, ~10%); that is the accepted price and it is stated, not hidden.

**Q. Is the docked/railed choice player state or derived?**

- **Decision:** Purely DERIVED from display size. There is no player collapse toggle in v1. The only comms UI state is ui_state::comms_peek (bool, default false), and it is meaningful only in railed mode — docked mode forces it false each frame.
- **Why:** A width-derived rect is deterministic, has no state the player can get stuck in, and keeps the band's geometry a pure function of disp. A user-collapsible dock would make the band's rect depend on hidden state at some widths and not others — the locally-clever option that reads as arbitrary later.

**Q. How does the Selection band's rect change, precisely?**

- **Decision:** band.x = shell_column_width(disp.x) + comms_dock_rect(disp).w; band.w = max(0, budget - dock_w); band.y and band.h unchanged (disp.y - 340, 340). Resolved widths: 1280x720 -> band 500 (was 556); 1600x900 -> 576; 1720x1080 -> 677 (was 996); 1920x1080 -> 811; 2560x1440 -> 1249. app.cpp's hand-rolled block at :2643-2654 is replaced by a single call to ui::selection_band_rect(disp).
- **Why:** One function owns the algebra so the band and the dock cannot disagree — the failure mode the current five-times-re-derived right edge invites. Keeping height and the flush edges fixed means only one dimension changed, which is the smallest possible perturbation to a band Ben tuned three days ago.

**Q. Does the fold-out ledger column lose any vertical budget?**

- **Decision:** No. foldout_column_rect() is untouched: {nav_pane_width, profile_panel_height, W - nav_pane_width, disp.y - profile_panel_height}. The comms dock starts at x = W, so column and dock are horizontally disjoint — no occlusion, no reflow, the BL-117 one-question-per-view splits stay valid verbatim.
- **Why:** Ben's fixed call, and the whole reason this option was chosen over hosting comms inside the column.

**Q. What IS a pinned item, concretely — and at what disclosure depth?**

- **Decision:** A pinned item is a compact WATCH CARD: a title row ([kind icon] name, then right-aligned [>] go-to and [x] unpin) over the shared ui::entity_summary stat block for that entity (draw_body_summary / draw_tile_summary / draw_building_summary / draw_market_summary / draw_unit_summary / draw_nation_summary / draw_corporation_summary). It is NOT the Selection band's per-kind action content.
- **Why:** The recon is decisive: the rich band builders (draw_selection_content, draw_tile_selection, draw_building_selection, draw_selection_action, draw_selection_facts) are entity-IMPLICIT — they all read ui.selected_entity — and they mutate singletons (card_resource_page bound by reference, card_stack, show_build_ledger, construction.pending_*). Hosting them twice needs entity threading through five functions plus per-host keying of three singletons, and BL-214 is about to redefine disclosure anyway. entity_summary is already entity-parameterised, already the sanctioned second-host path (draw_hover_card uses it), and LAYOUT.md's Ledger family conventions already MANDATE it for shared per-entity stat blocks. Pins are a watch list, not a second action surface; acting is one click away.

**Q. Do the content builders collide when hosted twice? If so, how is that fixed?**

- **Decision:** They do not, given the entity_summary choice — those builders contain exactly one widget id (BeginTable("market_summary") in entity_summary.cpp:212), emit no Button/Selectable/BeginChild, write no ui_state, and tolerate stale ids. The one real collision (two market pins sharing the table id) is fixed by wrapping every pin card in ImGui::PushID(static_cast<int>(entity)) / PopID(). No de-singletonising of ui_state is needed and none is done.
- **Why:** Choosing the depth that is already re-hostable turns an expensive refactor into a one-line PushID. That is the composable answer; threading entity ids through the band's dispatcher is a real change that belongs to BL-214, not to a layout re-plan.

**Q. How many pins maximum?**

- **Decision:** ui::pinned_items_max = 6. The panel scrolls vertically when the cards exceed the available height. When full, the Selection band's pin button is drawn disabled with the tooltip "Pin list full (6) - unpin one first."
- **Why:** The freed right-column slot is 336 x ~698 at 1720x1080 and 336 x ~338 at 1280x720; six cards fill the tall case and scroll at the floor. Six is a real working set but still scannable, and the cap fails LOUDLY (disabled + reason) rather than silently dropping a pin — LAYOUT.md's never-silent rule applied to an action instead of a figure.

**Q. How is a pin added?**

- **Decision:** A [pin] button in the Selection band's header button cluster, immediately left of go-to [>] and close [x]. To avoid adding it in three places, factor the cluster once: new ui::draw_selection_header_buttons(world&, ui_state&, entity_id, float bar_w, bool show_goto) exported from selection_panel.hpp, replacing selection_panel.cpp:1209-1218 (generic header, show_goto=true) and :599-604 (tile header, show_goto=false — the tile has no go-to today and keeps none). It is a TOGGLE: when the entity is already pinned the button renders filled in palette::pinned (amber) with the tooltip "Unpin", and re-clicking unpins. The drill header (selection_card.cpp:36-62) is left alone — a drill frame is not pinnable; pin its root tile instead.
- **Why:** Three structurally identical header copies were already a sync hazard; adding a fourth button to all three would make it a certainty. Toggle semantics are mandatory here under the standing toggle rule — the pin's active state IS visible, so re-clicking must undo it. palette::pinned already exists and has been unused since the Explorer was cut; this is the slot it was defined for.

**Q. Do pins survive a session or a save?**

- **Decision:** No. ui_state::pinned_entities is session-local view state, not serialised — matching ui::chat_state (BL-205 slice 1) and every other ui_state field.
- **Why:** ui_state is pure view state; nothing in it is serialised today. Persisting pins means putting player intent through the save seam, which is a serialisation-format change this layout item has no business making. It rides the same landing as chat serialisation (BL-202/BL-205 slice 2) when commands become world state.

**Q. What happens when a pinned entity is destroyed?**

- **Decision:** The pin is pruned silently. ui::prune_pins(const world&, ui_state&) runs at the top of draw_pinned_panel and erases any id whose selection_kind_of(w, id) == selection_kind::none. No tombstone, no notification.
- **Why:** SELECTION.md already sets the precedent — "treat a missing id as no selection". A demolished building's card disappearing is self-explanatory; a persistent "this was removed" row is noise in an ambient watch list. View-state only, so determinism is untouched.

**Q. Does clicking a pin select it?**

- **Decision:** Yes. Single-click on a pin card body sets ui.selected_entity and clears ui.selection_hidden_for (so the band opens on it). Double-click routes through ui::focus_on_entity — navigate. The explicit [>] button on the card does the same as the double-click, for discoverability.
- **Why:** This is exactly SELECTION.md's uniform click model (single-click selects, double-click navigates) extended to a new surface. Inventing a different gesture for pins would be the fourth answer to a question the project already answered once.

**Q. Does the minimap move, and how does the right column's vertical budget split?**

- **Decision:** The minimap does NOT move. The right chrome column keeps today's TWO-way elastic split: time panel at the top (content-derived time_h), the Pinned items panel taking the whole residual middle, and the minimap + lens bar locked to the bottom-right at mm_origin with mm_h = 0.75 * mm_w. Pinned items inherit the comms panel's exact rect: {right_chrome_left(disp), shell_margin + time_h + shell_margin, right_chrome_width(disp), minimap_rect(disp).y - shell_margin - y}.
- **Why:** The feared three-way split never materialises because comms LEAVES as pins ARRIVE — it is a swap, not an addition. The minimap's corner is the zoom-ladder ascend affordance and load-bearing muscle memory; moving it would move every golden for no gain and is outside this item's remit. Pins take the residual because they are the only elastic member (time is content-derived, the minimap is ratio-locked).

**Q. How does the comms panel re-lay-out for its new host?**

- **Decision:** The problem is vertical, not horizontal — at 1720x1080 comms goes from 336x698 to 319x340, i.e. essentially the same width but half the rows. Four changes in chat_panel.cpp: (1) the standalone TextDisabled("COMMS") + Separator is folded into the control row, recovering a text line plus a separator; (2) the two-line message stanza (TextWrapped day+speaker, then Indent + TextWrapped body) becomes ONE wrapped paragraph — dim `d%d ` then the speaker in identity colour then ": " via SameLine(0,0), then TextWrapped(body), no Indent — recovering ~40% of rows; (3) the SameLine channel tab chain (which has no overflow handling at all) becomes a single-row BeginCombo channel selector plus the "+" button, so channel count can no longer clip; (4) the new_group popup gets SetNextWindowSizeConstraints({220,0},{320,260}) with the corp checkbox list inside BeginChild("##grp_members", {0,160}) so it can no longer grow unbounded from a bottom-anchored popup.
- **Why:** Rows are now the scarce axis, so every fix buys rows. The channel combo is a cross-cutting selector and therefore explicitly EXEMPT from the toggle rule, so it costs no rule complexity; it also removes a real clipping bug rather than papering over it. All four changes stay inside the wrap-plus-vertical-scroll policy — no new text policy, no measured boxes.

**Q. Which container-vocabulary rows do the two new surfaces claim?**

- **Decision:** None new — the nine-container set is not extended. The comms dock and the Pinned items panel are both instances of container 1 (wrap to inner width, vertical scroll); LAYOUT.md's row 1 is renamed from "Fold-out ledger column" to "Fixed shell column / dock" and lists its three instances. The collapsed comms rail is an instance of container 8 (nav rail — icon-only, tooltips wrap).
- **Why:** LAYOUT.md's own rule is that new UI work lands in one of the nine rather than inventing a tenth. Both surfaces are scrolling text columns; declaring their policy up front means BL-215's audit inherits two compliant surfaces instead of two new offenders.

**Q. How is the five-times-re-derived right chrome edge handled?**

- **Decision:** A new src/ui/shell_metrics.{hpp,cpp} becomes the single home of the shell rect algebra: shell_margin, right_chrome_width(disp), right_chrome_left(disp), minimap_rect(disp), bottom_band_budget(disp), comms_dock_mode(disp), comms_dock_rect(disp), comms_peek_rect(disp), selection_band_rect(disp), pinned_panel_rect(disp, time_h). app.cpp's five independent derivations of disp.x - margin - mm_w (:2291, :2414, :2509, :2585, :2645) are repointed at it. shell_column_width / foldout_column_rect stay where they are and are consumed, not moved.
- **Why:** This item adds a fourth region to a shell whose right edge is already re-derived five times by hand; adding to that without fixing it guarantees a drift bug. Doing it FIRST, as a no-visual-change foundation task, means the goldens confirm it in isolation before any rect actually moves.

**Q. Where does the comms peek sit in the Esc precedence ladder?**

- **Decision:** Directly after show_system_menu and before the card_stack pop, in app.cpp's Esc chain at :1795-1804: confirm_exit_pending -> show_system_menu -> comms_peek -> pop card_stack -> hide selection -> open system menu.
- **Why:** The peek is the most transient thing on screen and it OVERLAYS the band, so it must clear before Esc reaches anything underneath it. Same reasoning that already puts the system menu ahead of the drill stack.

**Q. Does either new surface get a nav-rail slot?**

- **Decision:** No. Both are fixed shell chrome, not ledgers — so neither appears in close_all_panels / any_panel_open, and neither is governed by the toggle rule's ledger clause. The only toggle introduced is the pin button on the Selection band header (and the comms rail, which toggles the peek).
- **Why:** MENU.md's standing rule is that only BROAD ledgers earn a rail slot. Comms never had one (BL-205 was explicit) and pins are selection-driven, exactly like the Selection band, which SELECTION.md already exempts on the same grounds.

**Q. Stale artefacts the re-plan must clear as it passes.**

- **Decision:** Four, all named in the recon: the exp_* locals in app.cpp:2593-2596 (Explorer naming for comms) are renamed comms_*; the dead ledger_window_spawn / ledger_window_size in src/ui/ledger_chrome.cpp are left in place but the Tile Ledger is confirmed migrated (deletion belongs to its own cleanup, not here); LAYOUT.md:20-21's claim that the canvas "shrinks vertically to clear the Selection band" is corrected (it does not — the band overlays a full-window canvas); and the "~410 px at 1920" figure in both foldout_column.cpp:19 and LAYOUT.md:52 is corrected to 384.
- **Why:** Two of the four are stale statements that would actively mislead the next reader of the exact maths this item is rewriting. Fixing them costs nothing while the file is open; leaving them makes the new geometry doc read as unreliable.

items.title: Evolution to sapience - gate chain plus extinction radiations, between S7 Green and the civilisation gate
items.summary: The chain runs S5 Spark -> S6 Breath -> S7 Green, then S8 jumps straight to resource endowment and a five-requirement civilisation gate. Nothing between multicellular life and a toolmaker is generated - sapience is ASSUMED. This item fills that span with the same causal treatment BL-209 gave abiogenesis: a gate chain for the hard biological thresholds, plus a radiation step at each mass extinction that decides which body plan inherits the freed niches. SETTLED 2026-07-29 (Ben, generation Q&A - three rounds, twelve calls). Sibling of BL-210, which named this stage but designed none of it.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-29 (Ben, Q&A). Twelve calls settled across three rounds; the four load-bearing ones for this item are (a) HYBRID SHAPE - gates carry the thresholds, radiations decide the inheritor; (b) OFF-HOMEWORLD SAPIENCE FIRES BUT IS ALWAYS DEAD; (c) FIXED CAMPAIGN EPOCH, variable depletion; (d) FULL ORAL HISTORY, drilled, so the chain is readable rather than consumed into scalars.

## The problem being solved

PLANETOLOGY.md S8 opens by claiming it answers the life->civilisation link, and that the link 'is not metaphorical and not a tech tree'. It then delivers on that claim ONLY for the resource endowment - banded iron, fossil carbon, laterite, supergene copper, soil, limestone - each with a real chemical gate. The civilisation gate that follows is five PHYSICAL requirements (fire, ore grade, dense fuel, arable land, cheap bulk transport), every one of which is a property of the PLANET rather than of any organism.

So the model currently generates a world that COULD support a civilisation and then asserts one arrived. There is no generated answer to what the sapient species IS, why it arose, or what it descended from - and, per the payoffs below, four separate downstream systems want exactly that answer.

## Shape: gates, then radiations

Two interleaved mechanisms, running S7 -> the civilisation gate.

**The gates** reuse BL-209's seven-gate template verbatim as a structural pattern: each reads scalars already computed upstream, tests one threshold, and has a distinct, nameable failure state that produces its own archetype. Candidate cut, to be confirmed against the diagnostic test during the doc pass rather than fixed here:

| Gate | Question | Reads from | Fails into |
|---|---|---|---|
| S7b Multicellularity | Did individuality scale past the single cell? | S6 oxygen flux; S5g genome headroom | microbial-only world - petroleum but no coal, no fauna |
| S7c Nervous system | Did anything centralise sensing and action? | O2 budget (neural tissue is metabolically extravagant); predation pressure | sessile biosphere - a living world with no behaviour |
| S7d Terrestrial radiation | Did complex life leave the water? | S7 ozone column; land fraction; arable substrate | ocean-locked complexity - no fire, no metallurgy, ever |
| S7e Sapience | Did a lineage generalise rather than specialise? | radiation outcomes; climate variability; encephalisation cost vs food density | fauna world - rich, complex, no one to trade with |
| S7f Toolmaking | Could it manipulate, and did it need to? | body plan from the last radiation; S7's fire gate | sapient but handless - the sharpest failure in the set |

S7f is the one to watch on the 'name the decision' test - it may collapse into S7e. Same treatment BL-209 gave S5f Compartment: include it, and cut it first if tuning shows it never fires distinctly.

**The radiations** are what makes 'evolution that leads to humanity' a CONSEQUENCE rather than a die roll. BL-210 already promotes mass extinctions from biography flavour text ('252 Mya extinction, recovery took ten million years') to real branch points. This item gives that branch its mechanism: at each extinction the surviving clades are scored against the POST-extinction environment - the oxygen, climate and land state the chain has already computed for that epoch - and the best-fitting body plan radiates into the empty niches.

This is the K-Pg analogue made generative. Whether the world's eventual toolmaker descends from something warm-blooded and small, something reptilian, or something that never left the shallows is decided by which extinctions fired, when, and what the air was doing at the time. Nothing is drawn from a hat that upstream state did not already load.

## What the winning body plan decides (all four accepted)

Ben took every option offered; each must survive the diagnostic test on its own.

1. **Industrialisation timing.** The winner's traits set how quickly toolmaking becomes industry, which feeds S9's depletion scalar. This makes S9's stated inversion - 'a richer endowment industrialises EARLIER and is therefore MORE drawn down at campaign start' - a generated quantity rather than one authored constant. Directly serves the Era 0 -> Era 1 pressure premise.
2. **Endemic goods and fauna.** The surviving clades ARE the biological trade goods. BL-191's endemic-trade-good mercantile track (C -> D) currently has no generated source; this becomes it. Each body's biosphere history names what is uniquely worth shipping off it.
3. **Workforce and habitability.** The sapient species' physiology sets the baseline habitability tolerances and workforce response that POPULATION.md today consumes as assumptions.
4. **Arable and the food chain.** Which plant and animal analogues were available to domesticate sets arable yield and the shape of the food economy - feeding BL-190's consumption model and the agriculture chain (BL-166, BL-168).

## Off-homeworld: fires, but always dead

The sapience gate is NOT structurally blocked on other bodies. The chain runs honestly everywhere, and where it completes it yields a precursor civilisation that ENDED - ruins, relict infrastructure, artefact goods that feed payoff (2). Never a live actor, so this pulls in no diplomacy, AI or military scope.

Ben's rate statement, which is a tuning target and not a clamp: other bodies reach life RARELY and complex multicellular life VERY rarely. Sapience beyond that is rarer still. He explicitly flagged live precursor content as a possible future mode or DLC direction - file the thought, do not build toward it.

**Rarity is SWEEP-TUNED, NOT CLAMPED.** The gates stay honest and are never rejected for producing life; planetology_sweep measures observed frequency across seeds and the CONSTANTS are tuned until the rate matches the target. This is the homeworld rule's own discipline - constrain the inputs, never the gates - applied to the rest of the system. BL-219 owns the instrument.

## Fixed epoch, variable depletion

Every world arrives at the SAME technological moment. Industrialisation timing varies, and what it varies is the DEPLETION scalar and the endowment - not the tech level the campaign opens at. An early-industrialising world is more drawn down; a late one is richer and rawer; both start the campaign in the same near-future present.

This is the conservative call and it is deliberate. The prototype's entire economy assumes comparable starting conditions, and a variable arrival tech state would break every balance assumption in it. It also keeps the near-future premise intact.

## Presentation: full oral history, drilled

The eight-line biography cap stays as the SUMMARY - PLANETOLOGY.md's brevity-is-characterisation rule is load-bearing and untouched. Beneath it the whole chain is readable: radiations, extinctions, the body plan that inherited each time, and what it cost. Surfaced through BL-211's History ledger using BL-209's drill-down pattern.

The history is authored as entries in BL-208's append-only world log, NOT a parallel per-body structure. This is why BL-208 was pulled forward this session.

## Determinism

All of PLANETOLOGY.md 'Determinism & cost' applies unchanged. Specifically:

- **Fresh stage tags** for every new gate and every radiation sub-stream. Do not reuse; PLANETOLOGY.md already warns 0x4A71012u is folded twice in hard_coded_world.cpp.
- **Per-gate hashed sub-streams** are load-bearing, for the reason BL-209 gives: they are what lets a gate be added or retuned later without silently re-rolling every earlier one.
- **No bare transcendentals in gate paths.** Any rate curve (encephalisation cost, extinction severity, recovery time) is a binned lookup table, on the precedent of the radiogenic decay bins and BL-209's RNA hydrolysis table.
- **Clade scoring must be integer or fixed-point.** A floating-point argmax over trait vectors is a portability hazard and a tie-break nightmare; specify deterministic tie-breaking by clade id.

## Cost

Ben's ceiling, set this session: **up to 30 seconds per stage**, and generation is explicitly NOT to be invisible. The generated history scrolling past is accepted as part of the experience. This is a large loosening of the current implicit budget and it is what makes a real radiation simulation affordable at all. BL-219's sweep needs a reduced-fidelity mode so batch runs over thousands of seeds stay viable against this ceiling.

## Harness impact (tools/verify/planetology_harness.cpp)

| Group | Risk |
|---|---|
| R2 four bodies land in stated archetypes | AT RISK - new failure archetypes from the S7b-S7f gates need their own rows |
| R4 iron/coal antagonism | LOW - this item sits downstream of the S6 fork BL-209 already covers |
| R5 homeworld corridor 100/100 | AT RISK - five new gates plus radiations the homeworld must clear; acceptance will fall and reject-and-reroll must absorb it |
| R7 every knob moves its outcome | new assertions for whatever leans bias the radiations |
| R12 the trace (BL-209) | extended - radiation events join the molecular events in the same log |
| **R13 NEW - rarity** | observed life / complexity / sapience rates across a seed sample sit inside their target bands. Owned by BL-219, asserted here |

## Cut, by the diagnostic test

PLANETOLOGY.md: 'for every generated value, name the decision it changes. Anything that fails is deleted, not tuned.' Provisionally cut: **specific clade taxonomy** (naming orders and families is worldbuilding that changes nothing); **sexual reproduction as its own gate** (real, and invisible downstream); **intelligence as a scalar** (the gate is binary - a world has a toolmaker or it does not); **language origin** (belongs to BL-218's culture layer, and is not a planetology question).

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Whether S7f Toolmaking survives separation from S7e Sapience (see above).
2. How many extinction checkpoints - a fixed count, or emitted by the climate/tectonic history itself? The second is truer and harder to bound.
3. Whether 'fauna world' (S7e failure: rich, complex, nobody home) needs its own archetype or reads as an existing one.
4. Authority propagation: PLANETOLOGY.md is deliberately NOT edited by this entry. Per the standing rule the design lives here until the work lands.

Read PLANETOLOGY.md S7/S8 and 'Known weaknesses' in full, BL-209's gate-chain design as the structural template, and BL-210's checkpoint/branch/lean mechanism before promoting.

items.title: Land-derived culture regions, and nations formed over them - replaces Voronoi BFS territory placement
items.summary: Culture has no home anywhere in the generation layer. NATION_GENERATION assigns political character from an authored table over Voronoi BFS territory; BL-210 promises borders and character as OUTPUTS of a settlement history but names no mechanism. This item supplies it: culture regions clustered from the land itself, sub-national, with nations grown over that fabric. SETTLED 2026-07-29 (Ben, generation Q&A - three rounds, twelve calls). Sibling of BL-210, which named this stage but designed none of it.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-29 (Ben, Q&A). Four calls settled here: (a) culture is a DERIVED TRAIT VECTOR, not a simulated diffusion; (b) the unit is the SUB-NATIONAL REGION, not the nation or the city; (c) it is HIDDEN from the player, feeding diplomacy and the AI layer only; (d) it is FROZEN at campaign start.

## Ben's framing

'Cultures are tied to the land, and nations form.' He had no preference on generation ORDER and asked which was computationally cheaper. The answer, given the derived-vector choice, is cultures-first - argued below - and that is the direction this item takes.

## Why cultures-first is both cheaper and better

Because culture is DERIVED rather than diffused, a culture region is a single clustering pass over tile data the pipeline has already computed: terrain composition and landform, river connectivity (BL-170), coastline, arable share, ore provinces, and the biosphere endowment from BL-217. No temporal loop, no per-epoch iteration.

Nations-first costs that same clustering pass ANYWAY - the land does not change - plus a settlement simulation that runs blind to it and then retrofits. Strictly more work for a weaker result.

And cultures-first pays a structural dividend: it gives nation formation MEANINGFUL GROWTH SEEDS. Voronoi BFS today seeds arbitrarily and grows outward, which is why generated borders read as tidy blocks with no history. Seeded from culture regions and grown along the same land gradients, borders become an accident of politics over a pre-existing human fabric - which is what makes a map read as historical.

## The mechanism

1. **Cluster the land.** Culture regions emerge from a clustering pass over the tile map, bounded by the barriers that actually bound cultures: mountain ranges, deserts, open water, and the absence of arable land. River valleys and coastlines pull a region together; a watershed divide splits one. Region count is a function of habitable land area and its fragmentation, not an authored constant.
2. **Derive the trait vector.** Each region gets a small fixed-width vector read off its own land and endowment - maritime vs riverine vs steppe vs highland origin, arable share, ore access, isolation, and (from BL-217) what there was to domesticate. Deterministic consequence, no dice.
3. **Grow nations over it.** Settlement and conflict history grows polities seeded from culture regions. A nation may hold several regions; a region may be cut across by a border. That mismatch is not a bug - it is the generated source of internal friction and irredentist claims, and it is exactly what a Voronoi partition cannot produce.
4. **Derive corporate focus from the result.** CORPORATION_GENERATION's authored focus table is replaced by the industrial character the settlement history actually produced. GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise - a saturated nation-owned substrate with lean specialist corporations - must survive this unchanged IN SPIRIT; it is the constraint the rewrite answers to, not a casualty of it.

## What culture feeds (all four accepted)

1. **Trade friction and affinity.** Cultural distance modifies route cost, market access, or counterparty willingness. This also gives BL-161's embargo / exclusive-trade lever a generated reason to exist rather than an arbitrary one.
2. **Demand preferences.** Culture shapes consumption baskets and endemic-good demand (BL-191), so two identically-endowed markets behave differently.
3. **Labour and industry character.** Workforce availability and productivity, and which industries a nation actually grew - feeding the substrate premise and corporate focus derivation.
4. **Conflict propensity.** Drives war and collapse branching DURING generation (BL-210's historical-extinction checkpoint), and nation-level friction at campaign start.

## Hidden, but its consequences are not - and that is the design

Ben: 'the player doesn't see this - it's just for the diplomacy and hidden AI layers.'

The trait vector is never surfaced. There is no culture lens, no culture entry in the Selection band, no name for a region in the UI. What the player sees is BEHAVIOUR: this market wants that good, this counterparty is difficult, this border is tense. The cause stays opaque; the effects are everywhere.

This is a deliberate and coherent position - it makes culture an explanation the world HAS and the player must infer, rather than a stat block to optimise against. State it explicitly in NATION_GENERATION.md when the work lands, because a future session will otherwise 'helpfully' add the lens.

**Developer inspection is SWEEP READOUT ONLY.** No Generation Ledger overlay. Culture appears as aggregate numbers in the batch output (BL-219) and nowhere else. Accepted risk, recorded here: a single nonsensical region will be hard to spot without a visual. If tuning proves that painful, a dev-only overlay is the escalation - not a player-facing one.

## Frozen at campaign start

Culture is a generation output and never moves during play. This respects the standing deferral on nation behaviour (backlog.json BL-054) and keeps the entire feature inside the generation layer, with zero runtime simulation. Drift from player action was offered and not taken.

## Determinism

- The clustering pass must be deterministic and order-independent - a tile's region assignment cannot depend on iteration order. Specify the tie-break explicitly.
- Fresh stage tags for the culture and settlement sub-streams.
- Trait vectors are fixed-point or integer. No floating-point comparison decides a region boundary.
- Region count and assignment must be identical across the determinism harness's twice-generated world (BL-106).

## Cut, by the diagnostic test

**Language families, religion, art, values, and named cultures** are all cut. None changes a decision - the four payoffs above are served entirely by the trait vector, and a hidden layer gains nothing from flavour it never shows. Note also the standing position that belief systems are Fable's territory, not this project's.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Trait vector width and axes - the four payoffs constrain it, but the exact set is a doc-pass decision.
2. Whether the settlement/conflict history that grows nations is genuinely temporal (epochs, with BL-210's historical-extinction checkpoints firing) or a single scored pass. The checkpoint mechanism implies temporal; cost says check it.
3. How region-to-nation mismatch is represented in the data model, since it is the item's main structural payoff.
4. Whether Voronoi BFS is fully retired or retained as a fallback for bodies with no culture layer.

Read NATION_GENERATION.md and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md in full, GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise, and BL-210's settlement-stage sketch before promoting.

## UPDATE 2026-07-30

Step 1 of the mechanism above says region count is "a function of habitable land area and **its fragmentation**". **BL-221** (docs/lore/HISTORY.md Stages 0-2) is what generates fragmentation as a quantity: cradle count from arable/ocean/river connectivity, then conquest-cost and exit-cost scalars from the same terrain barriers this item clusters on. So the two interleave rather than stack - BL-221 produces the polity seeds and the fragmentation field, this item grows nations over them, and BL-221's Stage 2 line ("{n} realms confirm mutual borders") can only be written after that growth. Specify the interleave at doc-pass time.

Also: **BL-224** asserts the non-hegemony invariant in the harness (no nation holds more than X% of habitable land or of any strategic resource), which is the falsifiability this item's clustering currently lacks given its sweep-readout-only inspection call.

items.title: Whole-pipeline generation sweep - rarity targets, per-lean/per-branch cost, and the culture readout
items.summary: Rarity is sweep-tuned, not clamped - which makes the sweep load-bearing rather than a convenience. tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp samples seeds within the biosphere chain; this generalises it across the whole pipeline (continents -> biosphere -> evolution -> settlement -> culture) and adds the rarity bands BL-238's honest gates are tuned against. SETTLED 2026-07-29 (Ben, generation Q&A - three rounds, twelve calls). Sibling of BL-210, which named this stage but designed none of it.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-29 (Ben, Q&A). Filed as a separate sibling deliberately: folded into either BL-238 or BL-239 it would be the first thing cut under pressure, and it is the ONLY instrument that makes the 'tuned, not clamped' discipline actually enforceable.

## Why this is load-bearing now

Ben chose SWEEP-TUNED, NOT CLAMPED for how often the system's other bodies get life. That choice is only honest if the measurement exists. Without it 'rare' is a hope; the gates run, and nobody knows what they produce until a player complains that three moons grew forests.

The same argument covers BL-210's already-stated rule that no lean may be a dead end, now extended to branches - and BL-239's culture regions, which have NO visual inspector at all by Ben's call, making the sweep readout their only window.

## What it must measure

1. **Rarity bands.** Observed frequency across a seed sample of: any life, complex multicellular life, sapience, and completed-then-dead precursor civilisation - per body and per system. Ben's stated targets are qualitative (life rare, complexity very rare, sapience rarer still); the sweep's first job is turning those into numbers the constants can be tuned against.
2. **Per-lean and per-branch cost.** Today's sweep measures acceptance rate and per-lean cost within the biosphere chain. Extend to lean x branch-combination space across the whole pipeline, so a dead-end combination surfaces as a NUMBER rather than a bug report. This is BL-210's explicit ask: 'generate many worlds, to see what targets are best, and how to tweak the overall strategy.'
3. **Homeworld acceptance rate.** BL-238 adds five gates plus radiations the homeworld must clear, and BL-209 adds seven before that. Acceptance will fall and reject-and-reroll absorbs it - but per-lean cost must be re-measured so no preference becomes a dead end.
4. **Culture aggregate readout.** Region counts, trait-vector distributions, and region-to-nation mismatch rates. BL-239's only inspection surface.
5. **Generation time per stage.** Against Ben's 30s-per-stage ceiling. A stage that drifts past it should fail the sweep, not be discovered in a playtest.

## Reduced-fidelity mode

The 30s-per-stage ceiling and a thousand-seed batch are incompatible at full fidelity. The sweep needs a reduced-fidelity path that keeps every GATE and BRANCH decision exact while skipping expensive presentation-side work - the molecular event trace (BL-209), the narrative log entries (BL-208), and per-tile detail no gate reads.

**The invariant that makes this safe: reduced fidelity must produce IDENTICAL gate outcomes to a full run for the same seed.** That is itself an assertion the harness should carry - otherwise the tuning instrument and the shipped generator drift apart, and every number the sweep produces becomes a lie.

## Skill registration

Per CLAUDE.md 'Tool creation is skill creation', the extended sweep is registered in the verifier-headless skill so it is discoverable and re-runnable rather than a procedure someone remembers. It joins planetology_harness, chemistry_tables_harness, world_audit and world_determinism there.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Sample size, and whether it is fixed or adaptive (run until the rarity estimate's confidence interval closes).
2. Output format - the existing sweep's table, or something diffable so a tuning change's effect is reviewable.
3. Whether rarity bands become hard harness assertions (R13 in BL-238) or advisory numbers. Assertions are stricter and will fail loudly during tuning, which is arguably the point.

Read tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp as it stands, PLANETOLOGY.md 'Verification' and 'The homeworld: preferences, a strict floor, and reject-and-reroll', and BL-210's batch-tuning section before promoting.

## UPDATE 2026-07-30 - two more things to measure

The docs/lore/HISTORY.md ladder (BL-221/222/223) extends the pipeline again, and Ben's framing for it is a direct instruction to this item:

> "For now, we want data on what kinds of worlds are interesting, so it would actually be valuable to see many failure cases, and find out what parameters should be tweaked for interesting gameplay." (Ben, 2026-07-30)

So failure cases are **wanted output**, and this sweep is where they are counted rather than hidden. Two additions:

6. **Historical-ladder outcomes.** Distribution of cradle count, fragmentation, nation count, first-industrialiser identity, industrialisation date and per-nation drawdown across a seed sample - the numbers BL-221/222's constants get tuned against.
7. **Hegemony rate.** BL-224's N1-N5 are measured as a RATE across seeds, not enforced per world (constrain the inputs, never the gates). The build fails when the rate exceeds its threshold; an individual hegemon world is a data point, not a rejection.

Also pin the **nation-count band** here by measurement: HISTORY.md asserts ~45 nations, the build generates 14. BL-224's N1 cannot be written until this sweep says what the generator actually does.

items.title: Chart question log - every visual declares the question it answers and why, on demand, never as a leading tutorial
items.summary: Raised by Ben in the same session as BL-214's fold-model revision, as a correction of what he originally meant by 'asking interesting questions' in the UI. He explicitly rejected a leading-Q&A tutorial pattern (prototyped and then discarded in build_UI_example_4 - a pre-written list of questions the game answers on the player's behalf): 'Tutorials should never even tell a player what they should be asking / answering, only how to navigate all the information.' What he actually wants is narrower and more honest: each visual carries its own closed-by-default note stating the question IT answers and why that evidence justifies the answer - a standing self-declaration per chart, not a guided tour. He also named a second audience for it: himself, while designing - reading the log across a view lets him navigate the UI, notice where an interesting question has no chart yet, and judge when a question is too large to answer in one visual.
