items.title: The timing harnesses assume -O2 but CMakeLists sets no default build type, and no ctest TIMEOUT is set anywhere
items.summary: Found 2026-08-01 by the review barrier. econ_stability's timing assertions were measured at -O2 and carry thin margins (largest rung 0.29 ms against a 1 ms bound; exponent 1.28 against 1.5). CMakeLists sets no default CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, so a single-config Ninja/Makefile configure builds at -O0 and check.bat's --config Release is a no-op there - a 5-10x slowdown would fail ctest for build-configuration reasons rather than real regressions. Separately, data_creep_harness now runs 1500 ticks of the real world (~7 s) and econ_stability a 6-rung sweep, with no set_tests_properties TIMEOUT anywhere in the file.

items.title: Checkpoint/branch data model - where branch state lives and how a lean biases which branch fires (BL-210 split 1 of 3)
items.summary: Split out of BL-210's umbrella design (2026-07-31) as the first of three subject-doc passes it named as not-yet-settled. Extends BL-167's shipped preferences mechanism (eight axes, each a lean of any/low/mid/high, resolved by reject-and-reroll) so a lean can also bias WHICH branch fires at a checkpoint, not just narrow a sampling range within one round. Two checkpoint classes exist in the pipeline today only as narration: the mass-extinction branch (already dated in the S5-S8 biosphere biography, e.g. '252 Mya extinction') and the new historical-extinction branch (collapse/war/revolution at the settlement stage, BL-218's biggest new idea). Neither is wired to the lean system yet - both are pure classification with no bias hook. SETTLED 2026-08-02: branch state lives on the body generation state as an APPEND-ONLY ORDERED list of checkpoint_record{stage_id, branch_taken, seed_used, viability_result} — deliberately shaped identical to BL-208 eventual log so migration is a move, not a rewrite, without blocking this post-v0.1.0 chain behind a v0.3.0 item. seed_used is mandatory (a branch that cannot be replayed in isolation is not debuggable). A LEAN IS AN ELIGIBILITY FILTER, NEVER A WEIGHT — it removes branches from the proposal set and the survivors stay uniform reject-and-reroll, so BL-167 no-full-customization rule falls out of the mechanism rather than being enforced by taste; if a lean filters everything out the checkpoint REROLLS rather than falling back. Exactly TWO checkpoint classes with a stated admission rule (a checkpoint is where the outcome distribution branches, not where something interesting happens — the latter is a log entry). Viability floors are PER-CHECKPOINT predicates over ONE mechanism with a uniform (state)->bool signature.

items.title: Nations rewrite - territory, political character & wealth as outputs of a simulated settlement/industrialisation history, not Voronoi + random draw (BL-210 split 2 of 3)
items.summary: Split out of BL-210 (2026-07-31); per DEVLOG (2026-07-28) named as 'the biggest remaining piece' of the whole pivot. Replaces NATION_GENERATION.md's Pass 1-5 (Voronoi BFS seed/growth/merge, then an independently-random Pass 4 politics draw) with a settlement -> industrialisation -> 1900s stage: nation borders, ideology/expansionism/economic_focus, and resource-profile emphasis become OUTPUTS of a simulated history seeded by the continent/biosphere chain above (arable share, river connectivity, ore provinces, fossil geography - BL-210/BL-209's chains) rather than summed post-hoc from tiles or drawn independently at random. Directly answers PLANETOLOGY.md's own named gap: 'the pass hands nothing to nation or corporation generation... this is the largest missing connection.' This is where the 'historical extinction' checkpoint (BL-217) fires, and where the post-WW2 industrial grounding open item (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md, CORPORATION_GENERATION.md) finally gets a mechanism. SETTLED 2026-08-02: KEEP the BFS/growth machinery (BL-053 already tuned its size variance — real value) and replace only what drives it — seed on arable/river/coastal scores from the continents chain, then grow with weights driven by historical pressure so variance EMERGES rather than being dialled in. Political character gets a concrete per-axis derivation: expansionism <- border-contest integral, economic_focus <- dominant resource class of tiles settled DURING industrialisation, ideology <- industrialisation timing vs neighbours (first-mover trends market, late catch-up trends statist). The rupture checkpoint has three concrete transforms (collapse contracts territory and resets the industrial clock; war redraws the contested border and raises the loser expansionism; revolution flips ideology and leaves territory alone). BL-054 SPLITS rather than folding: its fragmentation half folds in (a settlement sim yields exclaves for free — the best argument for the deeper option), its runtime nation-AI half stays parked. Cheap alternative (Voronoi + richer narration) surfaced and rejected as the lying-figure problem.

items.title: Corporations rewrite - industrial focus as an emergent output of nation settlement history, not an authored focus table (BL-210 split 3 of 3)
items.summary: Split out of BL-210 (2026-07-31), the third and smallest of the three subject-doc passes - deliberately sequenced last since it consumes BL-218's nation-history output. Replaces CORPORATION_GENERATION.md's Pass 1-2 (nation assignment weighted by static economic_focus, then an independently-weighted focus draw) with focus/holdings that read as a plausible consequence of the home nation's settlement/industrialisation history, rather than a table lookup. Directly answers the two open items CORPORATION_GENERATION.md already names: 'post-WW2 industrial grounding for the asset mix' and, partially, 'nation-seeded privatisation'. SETTLED 2026-08-02: focus derives from the corp HOME PROVINCE industrialisation history, not a nation average — a nation average would make every corp in a nation alike and destroy the specialist premise, whereas per-province gives within-nation variety for free. The authored focus-weighting table is RETIRED as a per-corp bias (two mechanisms deciding one field is how it becomes unexplainable) and replaced by world-level REJECT-AND-REROLL against a diversity floor — a floor on the SET is not a quota on any MEMBER, so Pass 2 diversity-without-quota property survives, and it reuses the same idiom as BL-167 viability floors and BL-217 checkpoints. Post-WW2 grounding names a specific pattern: early industrialisers moved UP the value chain (refined/product-skewed corps), late ones stayed extraction-heavy — derivable from the industrialisation-timing scalar BL-218 already produces for ideology, so one mapping rather than new machinery. Nation-seeded privatisation gets its HOOK (an industrialised province with no corp in its resource class is now expressible) but the mechanism stays deferred as runtime nation behaviour.

items.title: history_event cannot date a year - a historical-epoch timestamp for the oral history log
items.summary: FOUNDATION for the HISTORY.md ladder (BL-221/222/223) and cheap enough to land alone. history_event (planetology.hpp:121) timestamps with `float gya` - billions of years before present. Every stage of the historical ladder is dated in YEARS ("-XXXX: First granary cities", "YYYY: The {nation} Charter Act"); 1450 CE is 5.1e-7 Gya, which will not sort, print, or survive tuning at float precision. Land the timestamp change before any historical stage emits a line, not during.

items.title: The pre-national history ladder - agrarian surplus, the enforceable promise, and fragmentation-with-connectivity (HISTORY.md Stages 0-2)
items.summary: The first half of the stage ladder in docs/lore/HISTORY.md (new, from Fable): Stage 0 agrarian surplus, Stage 1 the enforceable promise / Charter Age, Stage 2 fragmentation-with-connectivity. Fills the first part of the stage BL-210 named but designed none of ("Settlement -> Industrialisation -> 1900s"). SETTLED 2026-07-30 (Ben): the ladder is 100% DRIVEN, not narrated - Stage 0 cradle count drives fragmentation, which drives the region count and nation count BL-239 forms polities over. Sibling of BL-222 (Stages 3-4) and BL-223 (Stages 5-6).

items.title: The industrial history ladder - capital disciplines the sovereign, and the energy transition (HISTORY.md Stages 3-4)
items.summary: The second half of the docs/lore/HISTORY.md ladder: Stage 3 capital disciplines the sovereign (states become credit-dependent and therefore commitment-bound), Stage 4 the energy transition (fossil fuels break the organic ceiling; each seed gets its own Britain). Drives the S9 drawdown scalar - which is what makes PLANETOLOGY.md S9's stated inversion ("a richer endowment industrialises EARLIER and is therefore MORE drawn down at campaign start") a generated quantity instead of one authored constant. Also the mechanism the post-WW2 industrial grounding open item in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md has been waiting for.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-30 (Ben, HISTORY.md review). Sibling of BL-221; same "100% driven, failure cases wanted" call applies (see BL-221 for the quote and the determinism reading).

## Stage 3 - Capital disciplines the sovereign

Interstate competition (BL-221 Stage 2) makes states dependent on credit, therefore on merchants and bond markets, therefore forced into credible commitment. States that default or confiscate lose the next war.

HISTORY.md's lesson is the one that matters for the campaign premise: *"this is why the campaign's nations respect corporate property in 1960: their ancestors that didn't were outcompeted."* Without this stage, "nations tolerate corporations" is an assertion. With it, it is a generated outcome with named losers.

**What it drives:** a per-nation *commitment* / creditworthiness character, which feeds nation political character (today assigned by NATION_GENERATION.md's own pass) and the corporate operating freedom in CORPORATION_GENERATION.md. A nation that confiscated its way through this stage is one whose charters are worth less - a generated reason for the industrial-focus spread rather than an authored table.

**Its runtime echo is deliberately NOT in this item.** HISTORY.md asks that asset seizure carry a sentiment/credit cost consistent with this stage; nothing in `src/` implements seizure at all, and nation behaviour is deferred by standing rule. Filed separately as **BL-225**, parked behind Laws/Politics.

## Stage 4 - Energy transition

Fossil fuels break the organic-economy ceiling; growth compounds; wealth stops being zero-sum land. HISTORY.md: *"Coal-near-cities made Britain - endowment, not virtue. Once wealth compounds, conquest's return-on-investment collapses relative to trade's, which changes what war is FOR."*

This is the stage most sensitive to the endowment vector, and the cheapest to implement honestly, because the data already exists. PLANETOLOGY.md S8 already generates coal rank (only mid-bituminous cokes), petroleum, and the iron endowment with its oxic-weathering grade upgrade; nation resource profiles are already derived by summing tile deposits. So the pass can **name which nation industrialised first purely from tile data** - fossil accessibility and ore grade on owned tiles, against BL-221's bulk-transport and river connectivity (BL-170). *Each seed gets its own Britain.*

Keep PLANETOLOGY.md S8's counterweight visible: charcoal reduced iron at industrial scale for two millennia, so **coke gates cheap steel, not steel**. A coal-rich but non-coking world industrialises late and expensively rather than not at all - which is a far more interesting outcome than a binary, and is exactly the kind of failure case Ben asked to see more of.

Line: `"YYYY: {nation} lights the first coke furnaces of the {region} basin."`

## The payoff: S9 drawdown becomes generated

PLANETOLOGY.md S9 today takes `drawdown` as a player preference (0-0.95) and asserts the inversion - richer endowment industrialises earlier, therefore is more drawn down at campaign start. BL-238 already promised to make industrialisation TIMING a generated quantity from the winning body plan's traits. This stage closes the loop: **timing x endowment -> drawdown**, per nation and per resource, instead of one global scalar.

That is what turns Era 0 -> Era 1 into a *pressure* rather than a menu choice, which GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise asserts but does not currently generate.

Note the interaction to specify, not discover: the `drawdown` preference must become a **lean** biasing this outcome, not a value competing with it - the same reconciliation PLANETOLOGY.md § Open calls 5 demands for `deposit_scalar` vs the endowment vector. Two independent levers multiplying makes both uninterpretable.

## The post-WW2 grounding item, finally answered

GENERATION_STRATEGY.md and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md both carry an unsettled note: *"the focus->asset-mix patterns should be grounded in research on the post-WW2 industries that led to space-related capability, so a specialist's holdings read as a plausible pathway toward off-world reach rather than an arbitrary mix."* Stage 4's output IS that grounding - an industrial character derived from which fuels and ores a nation actually had, in which order. Close that open item as part of landing this one, or explicitly state why it stays open.

## Determinism

As BL-221. Fresh stage tags; integer/fixed-point scoring for the first-industrialiser argmax with an explicit tie-break by nation id; the rank and grade curves already exist as binned lookups from BL-167 and must be reused, not re-derived with transcendentals.

## Harness impact

`planetology_harness` gains assertions that (a) the first-industrialiser is a deterministic function of tile fossil/ore data, not of iteration order over `world.bodies` (an `unordered_map` - the sorted-walk rule in PLANETOLOGY.md § Determinism applies); (b) a coal-rich non-coking world still industrialises, late; (c) drawdown correlates with industrialisation date in the stated direction, across a seed spread. (c) belongs to BL-240's sweep if it is expensive.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Per-nation vs global drawdown. Per-nation is truer and is what the "which nation industrialised first" line implies, but the economy today reads one body-level endowment - check the cost before committing.
2. Whether Stage 3's commitment character replaces NATION_GENERATION.md's existing political-character assignment or feeds it.
3. How much of the depletion constants stay free parameters. PLANETOLOGY.md § Known weaknesses is blunt that "the depletion inversion is a design assertion dressed as a finding" - do not let this item quietly promote it to physics.

Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md Stages 3-4, PLANETOLOGY.md S8/S9 and § Known weaknesses, GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Open cross-doc items, and BL-221 before promoting.

items.title: The averted rupture - a Cold War that did not go hot as the origin of diplomacy, and the premise reframed for the nation-with-chartered-corps identity
items.summary: HISTORY.md Stages 5-6 as delivered by Fable assume a WW3-scale global rupture that already happened, and frame the whole ladder as answering "why is the player a corporation". Ben rejected both halves 2026-07-30: the near-catastrophe was AVERTED (a Cold War that did not go hot), and it is the origin of DIPLOMACY as a system; and the player identity is a nation with chartered corps (BL-094), so the thesis needs re-pointing. Three docs currently disagree on where the rupture sits - CONCEPT.md:51 puts it at Era 0's exit, ERAS.md's Era 0->1 gate is purely mechanical, HISTORY.md puts it in the past. DESIGN-OWED because the reframe changes the ladder's payoff stage, not just its wording. SETTLED 2026-08-02: the "three-doc disagreement" is FOUR-way — the table omits BL-087 Era reframe (2026-07-08), which is the newest dated design and explicitly re-reads ERAS.md three mechanical conditions as gating a QUEST TREE rather than the Era. With BL-087 in the table the contradiction dissolves: there are TWO ruptures, not one — a PAST averted near-miss (backstory, drives starting conditions) and a FUTURE seeded catastrophic event that ends Era 0 during play. So CONCEPT.md:51 is CORRECT and survives UNAMENDED, reversing this item owed action 2; only ERAS.md needs correcting, and BL-087 already owns that edit. The two bind thematically: the rupture averted then is not averted this time. Seeded with the shape canonical, confirmed. Deterrence ceiling is the MEMORY — a per-nation scalar, NOT a nuclear-equivalent object, which would be the largest scope addition in the ladder filed under a backstory item. Stage 5 drives all three candidates as per-nation scalars with named consumers. NR-025.
items.design:
DESIGN-OWED, opened 2026-07-30 from the docs/lore/HISTORY.md review. Two of Ben's answers landed here and both invalidate what the doc currently says.

## What HISTORY.md says today

**Stage 5 - The Rupture.** *"The WW3-scale global rupture that closes Era 0's backstory. Every claimant to hegemony fights; every one is exhausted, winners included."* Its framing rule is load-bearing by its own account: the event should discredit territorial conquest, leave corporations as the only actors with intact cross-border capacity, and create a deterrence ceiling forcing ambition into economic channels - *"that single framing answers, in one stroke: why the player is a corporation, why nations tolerate it, and why rivals compete through markets rather than armies."*

**Stage 6 - Saturation, 1960.** The saturated background economy is the *post-hegemonic condition*, not a neutral start. Expansion happens from saturation, not strength.

## Ben's two corrections (2026-07-30)

> "I think the backlog holds too many conflicting ideas, so my intent was a bit lost. I don't know precisely what you mean by Rupture, but the idea is that the player is a nation with chartered corps, no longer just a corporation. If the docs don't reflect that, please update. Specifically, cold war can be one example of an Era 0 which was averted, and we will use it as an example which caused diplomacy to really evolve and begin."

**(a) The catastrophe was AVERTED, not survived.** Not a WW3 that happened and exhausted everyone - a rupture that came close and did not fire. The 1960 epoch (ERAS.md) is already literally the Cold War, so this needs no invention: the world of 1960 is one that looked over the edge.

**(b) Its payoff is DIPLOMACY, not corporate primacy.** The averted catastrophe is what "caused diplomacy to really evolve and begin". This is a better fit for what the build actually has than the original framing was - BL-212 (nation-voiced public comms) shipped, BL-205 (channel-based corp chat log, diplomacy as communication) is designed at A/v0.2.0, and neither had a generated origin story. Now they do.

**(c) The identity is nation-with-chartered-corps.** This is already settled and already documented - **BL-094** (designed, parked F, v0.2.0): the player pivots to the nation as strategic actor owning research/military/intelligence, with the chartered corp as the economic actor, prototyped as one. ROADMAP § v0.2.0 carries it. So the docs DO reflect it; what does not is `docs/lore/HISTORY.md`, which was written against the older single-corporation identity, and `CONCEPT.md:4` which still reads *"corporate or nation-state entity. The exact form is undecided"* - a line BL-094 owns and which must not be edited ahead of the v0.2.0 cut (standing rule: authority docs propagate as part of landing the work).

**The reframe is a strict improvement, not a loss.** Stage 1's Charter Age is *already* about the sovereign-and-chartered-company bargain. Under the corporate identity the ladder answered "why is the player a corporation"; under the nation identity it answers **"why does a nation act through chartered corporations, and why does it tolerate their cross-border operation"** - which is the same causal chain aimed at a question the game actually asks.

## The three-doc disagreement to settle

| Doc | Says |
|---|---|
| `CONCEPT.md:51` | Era 0's *exit* "is not a quiet graduation; a 'WW3'-scale global rupture reshapes the world enough that a rapid space expansion becomes plausible" - a FUTURE event, during play |
| `ERAS.md` § Era 0 -> Era 1 gate | Three purely mechanical conditions (Rocketry research, Launchpad staffed, propellant reserve). No event at all |
| `docs/lore/HISTORY.md` Stage 5 | A PAST event, backstory closing Era 0 |

All three cannot stand. The averted-rupture reading resolves it cleanly and is the direction this item takes: **the near-miss is in the past** (it is why 1960 is multipolar, diplomatic, and corporate-tolerant), and **Era 0's exit stays mechanical**. Whether the exit ALSO carries a narrative beat is a separate, smaller call.

## What the doc pass owes

1. **Rewrite HISTORY.md Stages 5-6** for the averted rupture and the diplomacy payoff, and re-point § Purpose claim 3 and § The compact thesis at the nation-with-chartered-corps identity.
2. **Settle the CONCEPT.md:51 conflict.** Either amend it (it is not BL-094-owned text) or state why the future-rupture reading survives alongside the past near-miss.
3. **Decide seeded vs canonical** - HISTORY.md's own open question 1. Seeded (which nations nearly fought, over what, and what pulled them back) is consistent with the rest of the generation stack and with Ben's "100% driven" call on BL-221; canonical is cheaper to write quest and tech fiction against. Recommend seeded, with the *shape* canonical: every campaign has an averted rupture, the belligerents and the trigger vary.
4. **Decide the deterrence ceiling** - HISTORY.md open question 2. Does Kepler get an explicit nuclear-equivalent, or is the memory of the near-miss the whole ceiling? This is the one call here that reaches forward into Era 1+ conflict design (BL-157), so it is worth answering deliberately rather than by default.
5. **State what Stage 5 drives**, since BL-221/222 are both driven and this stage must be too. Candidates: the diplomatic posture each nation opens with; the conflict-propensity input BL-239 lists as payoff 4; the deterrence constraint that keeps Era 0 conflict economic. Anything that drives nothing is deleted, not tuned (PLANETOLOGY.md § Presentation).
6. **Stage 6 mostly already exists** - GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § economic premise (saturated substrate, lean specialists, live opportunity gap) and PLANETOLOGY.md S9 (drawdown) are Stage 6. The owed work is one causal sentence connecting them to the averted rupture, plus confirming BL-222's generated drawdown supersedes S9's authored scalar.

## Why this is design-owed rather than designed

BL-221 and BL-222 can be promoted on the strength of HISTORY.md as written. Stages 5-6 cannot: the doc's version is a WW3 that happened, aimed at a player identity the project has since moved past. That is a design conversation, not a wording pass - and per Ben's own note ("the backlog holds too many conflicting ideas, so my intent was a bit lost"), the value here is in *removing* a conflicting idea rather than adding one.

Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md Stages 5-6 and § Open questions, CONCEPT.md § Eras, ERAS.md § Era 0 -> Era 1 gate, BL-094 in full, and BL-205/BL-212 for what diplomacy currently is, before designing.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the disagreement is FOUR-way, not three, and the fourth doc dissolves it

### The table in this item is missing BL-087, and BL-087 is the newest dated design

This item tabulates CONCEPT.md, ERAS.md and HISTORY.md as three irreconcilable claims. There is
a fourth, and it changes the answer:

**BL-087's Era reframe (2026-07-08)** — *"Eras are catastrophic events on the world clock — e.g.
a war, a satellite/Kessler cascade. The world moves on whether or not the player is ready. Tech
can move faster than the Era clock but never opens an Era."* And explicitly: *"the ERAS.md
Rocketry + Launchpad + propellant condition set is re-read as gating a new quest tree."*

That is dated **later** than the ERAS.md gate model it supersedes, and under the newest-dated-wins
rule it governs.

### With BL-087 in the table, there is no contradiction to resolve — there are TWO events

The apparent conflict came from reading every mention of "rupture" as the same event. They are
two, at different times, doing different jobs:

- **A PAST averted rupture** (HISTORY.md Stage 5) — the near-miss that explains why 1960 is
  multipolar, diplomatic and corporate-tolerant. Backstory. Drives starting conditions.
- **A FUTURE seeded rupture** (CONCEPT.md:51, BL-087) — the catastrophic event on the world
  clock that ends Era 0 during play. Deterministic, dated per campaign, with a visible countdown.

**So CONCEPT.md:51 is CORRECT and survives unamended**, which reverses this item's owed action 2.
The only doc that needs correcting is **ERAS.md**, whose three mechanical conditions BL-087
already re-reads as a quest-tree gate — and BL-087 owns that edit when its work lands.

The two events are also thematically bound in a way that is worth keeping rather than
discovering: **the rupture that was averted then is not averted this time.** The backstory
establishes that these powers can pull back from the brink; the Era 0 exit is the occasion they
do not. That is a stronger premise than either event alone.

### 3. Seeded, with the SHAPE canonical — confirmed

The item's own recommendation, and it is consistent with Ben's "100% driven" call on the ladder.
Every campaign has an averted rupture; **which** nations nearly fought, over what, and what
pulled them back all vary by seed.

### 4. Deterrence ceiling — the MEMORY is the ceiling. No nuclear-equivalent object.

The call this item flags as reaching furthest forward, so it is taken deliberately:

- **An explicit nuclear-equivalent is Conflict-proper scope**, and BL-157 (settled today) is a
  deliberately minimal unit stub with no weapon systems at all. Adding a strategic weapon here
  would be the single largest scope addition in the whole ladder, filed under a backstory item.
- **A per-nation deterrence SCALAR is enough** to do the job the stage needs — constraining Era 0
  conflict to the economic, which is what keeps the prototype's premise intact. Derived from how
  close *that* nation came in the seeded near-miss.
- Nothing has asked for the weapon. The stage needs an *output the runtime consumes*, and a
  scalar is one.

### 5. What Stage 5 drives — all three candidates, as per-nation scalars

Per the diagnostic test (anything that drives nothing is deleted, not tuned), Stage 5 outputs:

1. **Opening diplomatic posture** — where each nation starts on BL-158's asymmetric sentiment
   table. Nations that nearly fought start lower with each other.
2. **Conflict propensity** — BL-239's payoff 4.
3. **The deterrence constraint** — from 4 above.

All three are per-nation (or per-pair) scalars derived from the seeded rupture, and all three
have a named consumer. Nothing is authored prose.

### 6. Stage 6 — confirmed

The generated drawdown from BL-222 **supersedes** PLANETOLOGY S9's authored scalar, on
newest-dated-wins and on driven-not-narrated. The owed work is the one causal sentence tying
GENERATION_STRATEGY's economic premise to the averted rupture.

### 1 & 2 restated

Action 1 (rewrite HISTORY.md Stages 5-6) stands, and is doc work at landing rather than a design
call. **Action 2 is discharged**: CONCEPT.md needs no amendment. ERAS.md's correction belongs to
BL-087.

Recorded as NR-025, because "CONCEPT.md is wrong" was the item's stated expectation and the
answer is that it is right.

items.title: Non-hegemony as an asserted generation invariant - no seed may produce a world-conquering nation
items.summary: The campaign premise makes three historical claims (docs/lore/HISTORY.md § Purpose); claim 2 - "~45 nations coexist; none can conquer the rest" - is the only one nothing checks. HISTORY.md calls Stage 2 non-hegemony "the single cheapest lore assertion with the largest downstream payoff". SETTLED 2026-07-30 (Ben): ASSERTED IN THE HARNESS, not left as narrative. A seed that hands one nation 60% of the habitable land silently falsifies the premise, and today nobody would find out until a playtest.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-30 (Ben, HISTORY.md review - "Asserted in the harness"). Per CLAUDE.md § Tool creation is skill creation, the check is authored as a harness assertion and registered in the `verifier-headless` skill, not run as a one-off.

## What is being asserted

HISTORY.md § Purpose claim 2 and Stage 2. The reasoning is worth keeping because it is what makes the assertion load-bearing rather than decorative: *"A hegemon can CHOOSE stagnation - suppress a technology by decree and it stays suppressed. Forty-five rivals cannot: a capability banned in one polity re-emerges next door."* Non-hegemony is not flavour; it is the precondition for markets, dynamic prices, and cross-border corporate operation - i.e. for the game.

## The assertions

Candidate set, thresholds to be pinned by measurement (BL-240) rather than chosen here:

| # | Assertion | Reads |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | Nation count sits inside a stated band | `nation_generation` output |
| N2 | No single nation holds more than X% of habitable land | owner_map + habitability |
| N3 | No single nation holds more than X% of any Era 0 strategic resource's accessible deposits | owner_map + deposits |
| N4 | Terrain barriers actually land on borders at better than chance | owner_map + terrain landform |
| N5 | The largest nation cannot cheaply reach the smallest - conquest cost above a floor | BL-221 Stage 2's conquest/exit scalars + BL-146 road/A* cost |

N2 is the minimum viable version and is worth landing alone if the rest slip. N3 matters more for the *economy* than N2 does - a nation with a monopoly on accessible coal breaks the market premise without holding much land. N4 is what makes BL-239's clustering falsifiable rather than merely plausible.

## The nation-count gap someone must own

HISTORY.md asserts **~45 nations**. The build generates **14** (BL-094: "the player IS one of the 14 generated Voronoi nations"), with `min_nation_tiles = 80` merging anything smaller (`nation_generation.hpp:51`). That is a 3x gap, and N1 cannot be written until it is settled: either HISTORY.md's number is aspirational and the band is 12-20, or the grid and merge threshold change. **Flag, do not silently pick** - a harness that asserts 45 against a generator that makes 14 is a red build, and one that asserts 14 quietly retires a premise claim.

## Failure is a report, not a reroll

Ben's BL-221 call - *"it would actually be valuable to see many failure cases"* - applies here. A seed that produces a hegemon should be **reported by the sweep**, not rejected by the generator. The harness assertion runs over a fixed seed set and fails the build if the RATE exceeds a threshold; it does not gate individual world generation. This is PLANETOLOGY.md's own discipline (constrain the inputs, never the gates) and BL-238's "sweep-tuned, not clamped".

That split is the important design point here, and it should be stated in the harness comments: **N1-N5 are tuning targets measured across seeds, not per-world preconditions.**

## Where it lives

`tools/verify/world_audit.cpp` already walks the generated world and already carries threshold assertions (its S2 forest+wetland balance threshold caught BL-210's continent bias being 3x too strong). N1-N4 are natural additions. The per-seed RATE aggregation belongs in `planetology_sweep.cpp` under BL-240, which is already extending to whole-pipeline measurement.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. The nation-count band (see above). Blocking for N1 only.
2. Thresholds for N2/N3 - measure first, per Ben's standing "measure before reshaping".
3. Whether N5 is affordable, given it needs BL-221's conquest-cost scalars and an A* pass. Cut it first if not.
4. Whether a hegemon world gets a named archetype the way a dead body does. A "Hegemony" outcome that the sweep counts is more useful than an assertion failure with no name.

Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md § Purpose and Stage 2, tools/verify/world_audit.cpp as it stands, BL-240, and NATION_GENERATION.md before promoting.

items.title: Asset seizure costs the seizing nation - sentiment and credit access, not a free confiscation
items.summary: The one runtime mechanic docs/lore/HISTORY.md asks for: Stage 3 ("capital disciplines the sovereign") argues nations respect corporate property in 1960 because their ancestors that confiscated were outcompeted - so seizure must exist and must COST the seizer in sentiment and credit access. Progressive loss rather than a lose screen, mirroring the historical norm that sovereigns squeezed companies far more often than they destroyed them. Seizure is named as a loss vector in CONCEPT.md:41 and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md:21 but exists NOWHERE in src/. FILED 2026-07-30 (Ben: "file it, parked for Laws/Politics") so the claim is not lost; parked because nation behaviour is deferred by standing rule. SETTLED 2026-08-02 (two of three blockers settled the same day): sentiment is BL-158 asymmetric per-pair scalar, and a seizure moves sentiment[observer][seizer] down for EVERY observer weighted by that observer exposure — so an uninvested nation barely reacts and a heavily invested one reacts hard. Credit access is a RATE, not a ceiling (invisible until hit) or a refusal (a cliff that converts progressive loss into the single failure state CONCEPT forbids) — and it needs NO new channel, because BL-262 already routes capital standing into credit terms via BL-073, so seizure travels the same path. Symmetrical, per standing rule and because BL-094 makes the player the same entity kind. YES, BL-222 Stage 3 commitment character sets starting sentiment and credit standing — otherwise the generated history hands the runtime nothing and the stage is decorative. Now DESIGNED AND WAITING on BL-094, not design-owed.
items.design:
DESIGN-OWED, filed 2026-07-30 from the docs/lore/HISTORY.md review. Parked deliberately - this is recorded so the ladder's single runtime claim survives, not queued.

## The claim

HISTORY.md Stage 3, § Game-mechanical echo: *"Asset seizure exists but is costly to the seizing nation (sentiment, credit access). Progressive loss instead of a lose screen mirrors the historical norm: sovereigns squeezed companies far more often than they destroyed them."*

This is the mechanical consequence of the stage's lesson - if confiscation were free, the generated history that produced commitment-bound sovereigns would be contradicted by the runtime every time a nation seized something.

## Current state of the build

- `CONCEPT.md:41` - *"Losing ground, going bankrupt, or having assets seized are impactful and progressive forms of defeat"*, and § Bankruptcy and seizure names financial collapse and military takeover as the two loss vectors.
- `CORPORATION_GENERATION.md:21` - a home nation may *"seize the corporation's domestic assets"*.
- `src/` - **nothing.** No seizure, no sentiment, no credit access, no nation-initiated action of any kind on player assets. Nation behaviour beyond the data-model minimum is prohibited by standing rule; the only sanctioned exceptions are BL-079's narrow per-building corp agency and BL-181's workforce dial.

So this is not a gap in an existing mechanic; it is a mechanic that does not exist yet, with a design constraint attached in advance.

## Why parked, and what it waits on

| Requires | Why |
|---|---|
| **BL-155** Laws & policy surface (design-owed, v0.1.2) | seizure is a policy act and needs a law surface to be taken from |
| **BL-158** Politics data-model stub (design-owed, v0.1.5) | sentiment has to live somewhere |
| **BL-094** nation-as-strategic-actor (designed, parked, v0.2.0) | under the nation identity the player can be the SEIZER as well as the seized, which is the whole reason the cost matters - a cost only ever paid by AI nations is invisible |

BL-094 is the important one. A seizure mechanic designed while the player is purely a corporation is a mechanic the player only ever suffers. Designed after the pivot, it is a lever with a price - which is what Stage 3 is actually about.

## What the design pass owes

1. What sentiment IS - whose opinion, tracked at what grain (nation-to-nation, nation-to-corp, market-level), and what it changes. Anything it does not change is deleted, not tuned.
2. What "credit access" means against the existing budget system (`src/world/budget_system.*`) - a rate, a ceiling, or a refusal.
3. Whether the cost is symmetrical (standing rule: symmetrical rules, and under BL-094 the player is the same kind of entity as its rivals).
4. Whether BL-222 Stage 3's generated per-nation commitment character sets each nation's STARTING sentiment and credit standing - it should, or the generated history hands nothing to the runtime and the stage is decorative.

Do not promote ahead of BL-155 and BL-158. Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md Stage 3, CONCEPT.md § Bankruptcy and seizure, and BL-094 before designing.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the four owed answers. Still parked on BL-094.

Two of this item's three blockers were settled today (BL-155 laws, BL-158 politics), so the
design pass can be run even though promotion still waits on BL-094.

### 1. What sentiment IS — answered by BL-158

Settled today: **asymmetric per-pair `sentiment[from][to]`**, a bounded fixed-point scalar,
nation-to-nation. This item was one of the two reasons that asymmetry was chosen — a seizure is
directional, and every observer reacts differently.

**A seizure moves `sentiment[observer][seizer]` down for every observer, weighted by that
observer's exposure** (assets held in the seizing nation's territory, trade dependence on it).
A nation with nothing at stake barely reacts; one heavily invested reacts hard. That is the
mechanism by which "sovereigns squeezed companies far more often than they destroyed them"
becomes a runtime pressure rather than a claim.

Per the item's own rule — anything sentiment does not change is deleted, not tuned — sentiment
must feed licence cost/availability (BL-054) and credit standing (below). Those are its two
consumers; if either is cut, sentiment's grain shrinks with it.

### 2. Credit access is a RATE, not a ceiling and not a refusal

- **Refusal** is a cliff — binary, unplayable-around, and it converts a progressive cost into
  the single failure state CONCEPT explicitly forbids.
- **A ceiling** is invisible until you hit it, so it teaches nothing until it is too late.
- **A rate** is continuously legible, composes with **BL-073's existing debt interest**, and
  degrades gradually — which is exactly the "progressive loss instead of a lose screen" the
  HISTORY.md claim is about.

**And it needs no new channel.** BL-262 (settled today) already routes a capital standing into
credit terms via BL-073. Seizure cost travels the **same** channel: it moves the seizer's
standing, and standing already prices borrowing. One mechanism, two causes.

### 3. Symmetrical — yes

Standing rule, and under BL-094 the player is the same kind of entity as its rivals. A cost only
AI nations pay is invisible, which the item already identifies as the reason BL-094 is the
important blocker.

### 4. YES — BL-222 Stage 3's commitment character sets starting sentiment and credit standing

The item's own leaning, confirmed, and the argument is decisive: **if generated history does not
hand the runtime a starting value, the stage is decorative.** A nation generated as
commitment-bound (reliably honours contracts) starts with better credit standing and higher
sentiment from trading partners; one generated as expropriation-prone starts worse.

That is the whole point of the ladder being "driven, not narrated" — it must produce numbers the
runtime consumes.

### Still parked

`requires` BL-094 is unchanged and still binding. This is now **designed and waiting**, not
design-owed — do not promote before the nation pivot.

items.title: Continent lens — put the tectonic plates back on the map
items.summary: A tenth strip lens showing the tectonic plates from BL-210's Continents/Drift pass: per-plate categorical tint plus a pale lift on every tile that touches another plate. Low-friction by design — the lens shell is the settled nine-lens pattern (enum + glyph + tint branch + key), and the only real work is DATA RETENTION: run_continents computed a per-tile Voronoi plate assignment, folded its height bias into Pass 1's heightmap, and then dropped it, so by the time a tile exists the plate that raised it is unreadable from the terrain. Fix is to return the plate field and retain it on the generation report (presentation data, off the serialisation seam), not to re-derive or persist it.
